`max effort → 5+5 angles × 8 candidates → 1-vote verify → sweep → ≤15 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at maximum effort: catch every real bug. At
this level, catching real bugs matters more than avoiding false positives — a
missed bug ships. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (5 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 8 each)

Run **10 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 8 candidate findings**. Do NOT let one angle's conclusions
suppress another's — if two angles flag the same line for different reasons,
record both.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Angle D — language-pitfall specialist

Scan for the classic pitfalls of the diff's language/framework — for example:
JS falsy-zero, `==` coercion, closure-captured loop var; Python mutable default
args, late-binding closures; Go nil-map write, range-var capture; SQL injection;
timezone/DST drift; float equality. Flag any instance the diff introduces.

### Angle E — wrapper/proxy correctness

When the PR adds or modifies a type that wraps another (cache, proxy, decorator,
adapter): check that every method routes to the wrapped instance and not back
through a registry/session/global — e.g. a caching provider holding a
`delegate` field that resolves IDs via `session.get(...)` instead of
`delegate.get(...)` will re-enter the cache or recurse. Also check that the
wrapper forwards all the methods the callers actually use.

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, 3-state)

Dedup candidates that point at the same line/mechanism, keeping the one with
the most concrete failure scenario. For each remaining candidate, run **one
verifier** via the Agent tool: give it the diff, the relevant
file(s), and the candidate, and have it return exactly one of:

- **CONFIRMED** — can name the inputs/state that trigger it and the wrong
  output or crash. Quote the line.
- **PLAUSIBLE** — mechanism is real, trigger is uncertain (timing, env,
  config). State what would confirm it.
- **REFUTED** — factually wrong (code doesn't say that) or guarded elsewhere.
  Quote the line that proves it.

Keep candidates where the vote is CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE.

This is recall mode — a single non-REFUTED vote carries the finding. Do NOT
drop on uncertainty.

## Phase 3 — Sweep for gaps

Run **one more finder** as a fresh reviewer who has the verified list. Re-read
the diff and enclosing functions looking ONLY for defects not already listed.
Do not re-derive or re-confirm anything already there — the job is gaps. Focus
on what the first pass tends to miss: moved/extracted code that dropped a guard
or anchor; second-tier footguns (dataclass default evaluated once, `hash()`
non-determinism, lock-scope shrink, predicate methods with side effects);
setup/teardown asymmetry in tests; config defaults flipped.

Surface **up to 8 additional candidates**, each naming a defect not already on
the list. If nothing new, return an empty sweep — do not pad.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 15 objects:

[

    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 15 survive, keep the 15 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`.

23	/****************************************************************************
24	 * RV1126B HPMCU IRQ dispatch for NuttX
25	 *
26	 * This file implements the RISC-V interrupt dispatch logic for the
27	 * RV1126B HPMCU.  The SCR1 core uses the IPIC (CSR 0xbf0..0xbf7) for
28	 * interrupt prioritization and EOI/SOI handshaking, and the INTMUX
29	 * for external interrupt routing.
30	 *
31	 * Dispatch flow:
32	 *   1. Trap entry (rv1126b_head.S g_traps) saves context and calls
33	 *      riscv_dispatch_irq(mcause, regs).
34	 *   2. riscv_dispatch_irq() identifies the interrupt type and:
35	 *      - For timer interrupts (mcause=7): calls up_timer_int()
36	 *        and returns regs.
37	 *      - For external interrupts (mcause=11): scans INTMUX status
38	 *        registers to find the active IRQs, then dispatches each
39	 *        via riscv_doirq(irq, regs) (which handles context switch
40	 *        bookkeeping), wrapped by IPIC SOI/EOI.
41	 *   3. The returned regs pointer is used by the assembly trap exit
42	 *      to restore the (possibly switched) context.
43	 ****************************************************************************/
44

89	 *
90	 ****************************************************************************/

92	static inline void rv1126b_ipic_soi(void)

95	}

99	 *

102	 *   interrupt processing.  Any value can be written.
103	 *
104	 ****************************************************************************/
105

107	{

109	}

111	/****************************************************************************
112	 * Name: rv1126b_get_active_irq
113	 *
114	 * Description:
115	 *   Scan the INTMUX status registers to find the highest-priority
116	 *   active (pending and enabled) IRQ.
117	 *
118	 * Returned Value:
119	 *   IRQ number (0..255), or -1 if no active IRQ is found.
120	 *
121	 ****************************************************************************/
122	
123	static int rv1126b_get_active_irq(void)
124	{
125	  int i;
126	  unsigned int status;
127	
128	  for (i = 0; i < INTMUX_NGROUPS; i++)
129	    {
130	      status = getreg32(RV1126B_INTMUX_BASE +
131	                         RV1126B_INTMUX_STATUS_OFFSET +
132	                         (i * RV1126B_INTMUX_GROUP_STRIDE));
133	      if (status != 0)
134	        {
135	          /* Find the lowest-numbered (highest priority) set bit */
136	
137	          int bit = __builtin_ctz(status);
138	          return i * INTMUX_IRQS_PER_GROUP + bit;
139	        }
140	    }
141	
142	  return -1;
143	}

149	/****************************************************************************
150	 * Name: riscv_dispatch_irq
151	 *
152	 * Description:
153	 *   Dispatch an interrupt based on the mcause value.
154	 *
155	 *   This function is called from the NuttX RISC-V common interrupt
156	 *   handling path (riscv_doirq -> riscv_dispatch_irq) when the mcause
157	 *   indicates an interrupt (bit 31 set).
158	 *
159	 *   For the RV1126B HPMCU:
160	 *     - mcause == 7  (IRQ_M_TIMER): machine timer interrupt
161	 *     - mcause == 11 (IRQ_M_EXT):   machine external interrupt
162	 *       (routed through INTMUX)
163	 *
164	 * Input Parameters:
165	 *   mcause - The value of the mcause CSR
166	 *   regs   - Pointer to the saved register context
167	 *
168	 * Returned Value:
169	 *   Pointer to the (possibly new) register context after dispatch.
170	 *
171	 ****************************************************************************/
172	
173	void *riscv_dispatch_irq(uintptr_t mcause, uintreg_t *regs)
174	{
175	  uintptr_t cause;
176	
177	  if ((mcause & MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT) == 0)
178	    {
179	      /* Synchronous exceptions must go through riscv_doirq() so NuttX can
180	       * advance mepc for ecall and handle context switching properly.
181	       */
182	
183	      regs = riscv_doirq((int)mcause, regs);
184	      return regs;
185	    }
186	
187	  /* Interrupt: strip the interrupt bit to get the cause code */
188	
189	  cause = mcause & ~MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT;
190	
191	  if (cause == IRQ_M_TIMER)
192	    {
193	      /* Machine timer interrupt -- call the NuttX timer handler */
194	
195	      up_timer_int();
196	    }
197	  else if (cause == IRQ_M_EXT)
198	    {
199	      /* Machine external interrupt -- scan INTMUX for active IRQs */
200	
201	      int irq;
202	
203	      /* Signal IPIC Start of Interrupt */
204	
205	      rv1126b_ipic_soi();
206	
207	      /* Scan for active IRQs -- handle all pending IRQs in this group */
208	
209	      while ((irq = rv1126b_get_active_irq()) >= 0)
210	        {
211	          /* Dispatch through the NuttX IRQ dispatch table.
212	           * riscv_doirq() handles context switch bookkeeping and
213	           * returns the (possibly updated) regs pointer.
214	           */
215	
216	          regs = riscv_doirq(irq, regs);
217	        }
218	
219	      /* Signal IPIC End of Interrupt */
220	
221	      rv1126b_ipic_eoi();
222	    }
223	  else
224	    {
225	      /* Unexpected interrupt cause -- spin */
226	
227	      for (; ; );
228	    }
229	
230	  return regs;
231	}

146	 *
147	 * Description:
148	 *   Initialize the HPMCU DCache:
149	 *   - Configure the uncache address region via GRF_SYS so that
150	 *     memory-mapped peripherals (0x20000..0x23000) bypass the cache.
151	 *   - Enable DCache with store buffer (stb_entry=7, timeout enabled).
152	 *   - Wait for cache initialization to complete.
153	 *   - Clear the cache bypass bit to enable caching.
154	 *
155	 *   Note: Do not access uninitialized global variables before this
156	 *   function completes, as BSS must already be zeroed.

160	static bool rv1126b_dcache_init(void)
161	{
162	  volatile uint32_t *grf_cache_start =
163	    (volatile uint32_t *)GRF_HPMCU_CACHE_ADDR_START;
164	  volatile uint32_t *grf_cache_end =
165	    (volatile uint32_t *)GRF_HPMCU_CACHE_ADDR_END;
166	  volatile uint32_t *dcache_ctrl =
167	    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_CACHE_CTRL;
168	  volatile uint32_t *dcache_status =
169	    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_CACHE_STATUS;
170	  volatile uint32_t *dcache_stb =
171	    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_STB_TIMEOUT_CTRL;
172	  volatile uint32_t timeout = RV1126B_DIAG_POLL_TIMEOUT;
173	
174	  /* Set the uncache region to cover peripheral address space */
175	
176	  *grf_cache_start = 0x20000;
177	  *grf_cache_end   = 0x23000;
178	
179	  /* Enable DCache: cache_en=1, stb_entry=7, stb_timeout_en=1 */
180	
181	  *dcache_ctrl |= DCACHE_CACHE_EN_BIT |
182	                  DCACHE_CACHE_ENTRY_THRESH |
183	                  DCACHE_STB_TIMEOUT_EN_BIT;
184	
185	  /* Enable store buffer timeout */
186	
187	  *dcache_stb = 1;
188	
189	  /* Wait for cache initialization to finish */
190	
191	  while ((*dcache_status & DCACHE_INIT_FINISH_BIT) == 0)
192	    {
193	      if (timeout-- == 0)
194	        {
195	          return false;
196	        }
197	    }
198	
199	  /* Clear bypass to enable caching */
200	
201	  *dcache_ctrl &= ~DCACHE_CACHE_BYPASS_BIT;
202	  return true;
203	}

23	/****************************************************************************
24	 * RV1126B HPMCU IRQ dispatch for NuttX
25	 *
26	 * This file implements the RISC-V interrupt dispatch logic for the
27	 * RV1126B HPMCU.  The SCR1 core uses the IPIC (CSR 0xbf0..0xbf7) for
28	 * interrupt prioritization and EOI/SOI handshaking, and the INTMUX
29	 * for external interrupt routing.
30	 *
31	 * Dispatch flow:
32	 *   1. Trap entry (rv1126b_head.S g_traps) saves context and calls
33	 *      riscv_dispatch_irq(mcause, regs).
34	 *   2. riscv_dispatch_irq() identifies the interrupt type and:
35	 *      - For timer interrupts (mcause=7): calls up_timer_int()
36	 *        and returns regs.
37	 *      - For external interrupts (mcause=11): scans INTMUX status
38	 *        registers to find the active IRQs, then dispatches each
39	 *        via riscv_doirq(irq, regs) (which handles context switch
40	 *        bookkeeping), wrapped by IPIC SOI/EOI.
41	 *   3. The returned regs pointer is used by the assembly trap exit
42	 *      to restore the (possibly switched) context.
43	 ****************************************************************************/

114	 * Description:
115	 *   Scan the INTMUX status registers to find the highest-priority
116	 *   active (pending and enabled) IRQ.
117	 *
118	 * Returned Value:
119	 *   IRQ number (0..255), or -1 if no active IRQ is found.
120	 *

123	static int rv1126b_get_active_irq(void)
124	{
125	  int i;
126	  unsigned int status;
127	
128	  for (i = 0; i < INTMUX_NGROUPS; i++)
129	    {
130	      status = getreg32(RV1126B_INTMUX_BASE +
131	                         RV1126B_INTMUX_STATUS_OFFSET +
132	                         (i * RV1126B_INTMUX_GROUP_STRIDE));
133	      if (status != 0)
134	        {
135	          /* Find the lowest-numbered (highest priority) set bit */
136	
137	          int bit = __builtin_ctz(status);
138	          return i * INTMUX_IRQS_PER_GROUP + bit;
139	        }
140	    }
141	
142	  return -1;

149	/****************************************************************************
150	 * Name: riscv_dispatch_irq
151	 *
152	 * Description:
153	 *   Dispatch an interrupt based on the mcause value.
154	 *
155	 *   This function is called from the NuttX RISC-V common interrupt
156	 *   handling path (riscv_doirq -> riscv_dispatch_irq) when the mcause
157	 *   indicates an interrupt (bit 31 set).
158	 *
159	 *   For the RV1126B HPMCU:
160	 *     - mcause == 7  (IRQ_M_TIMER): machine timer interrupt
161	 *     - mcause == 11 (IRQ_M_EXT):   machine external interrupt
162	 *       (routed through INTMUX)
163	 *
164	 * Input Parameters:
165	 *   mcause - The value of the mcause CSR
166	 *   regs   - Pointer to the saved register context
167	 *
168	 * Returned Value:
169	 *   Pointer to the (possibly new) register context after dispatch.
170	 *
171	 ****************************************************************************/
172	
173	void *riscv_dispatch_irq(uintptr_t mcause, uintreg_t *regs)
174	{
175	  uintptr_t cause;
176	
177	  if ((mcause & MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT) == 0)
178	    {
179	      /* Synchronous exceptions must go through riscv_doirq() so NuttX can
180	       * advance mepc for ecall and handle context switching properly.
181	       */
182	
183	      regs = riscv_doirq((int)mcause, regs);
184	      return regs;
185	    }
186	
187	  /* Interrupt: strip the interrupt bit to get the cause code */
188	
189	  cause = mcause & ~MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT;
190	
191	  if (cause == IRQ_M_TIMER)
192	    {
193	      /* Machine timer interrupt -- call the NuttX timer handler */
194	
195	      up_timer_int();
196	    }
197	  else if (cause == IRQ_M_EXT)
198	    {
199	      /* Machine external interrupt -- scan INTMUX for active IRQs */
200	
201	      int irq;
202	
203	      /* Signal IPIC Start of Interrupt */
204	
205	      rv1126b_ipic_soi();
206	
207	      /* Scan for active IRQs -- handle all pending IRQs in this group */
208	
209	      while ((irq = rv1126b_get_active_irq()) >= 0)
210	        {
211	          /* Dispatch through the NuttX IRQ dispatch table.
212	           * riscv_doirq() handles context switch bookkeeping and
213	           * returns the (possibly updated) regs pointer.
214	           */
215	
216	          regs = riscv_doirq(irq, regs);

218	
219	      /* Signal IPIC End of Interrupt */

221	      rv1126b_ipic_eoi();
222	    }
223	  else
224	    {
225	      /* Unexpected interrupt cause -- spin */
226	
227	      for (; ; );
228	    }
229	
230	  return regs;

51	 * Pre-processor Definitions
52	 ****************************************************************************/

54	/* GRF_SYS HPMCU cache address region registers.
55	 * These configure the uncache region for memory-mapped peripherals.
56	 * From RV1126B TRM: GRF_SYS at 0x20100000 (MCU view).
57	 */
58	
59	#define GRF_SYS_MCU_BASE            RV1126B_GRF_SYS_BASE
60	#define GRF_HPMCU_CACHE_ADDR_START  (GRF_SYS_MCU_BASE + 0x001C)
61	#define GRF_HPMCU_CACHE_ADDR_END    (GRF_SYS_MCU_BASE + 0x0020)
62	
63	/* DCACHE control registers.
64	 * From RV1126B memory map: DCACHE at 0x209D0000 (MCU view).
65	 */
66	
67	#define DCACHE_BASE                 RV1126B_DCACHE_BASE
68	#define DCACHE_CACHE_CTRL       (DCACHE_BASE + 0x0000)
69	#define DCACHE_CACHE_STATUS     (DCACHE_BASE + 0x0030)
70	#define DCACHE_STB_TIMEOUT_CTRL (DCACHE_BASE + 0x000C)
71	
72	/* DCACHE_CACHE_CTRL bit fields */
73	
74	#define DCACHE_CACHE_EN_BIT         (1 << 0)
75	#define DCACHE_CACHE_ENTRY_THRESH   (7 << 8)   /* stb_entry = 7 */
76	#define DCACHE_STB_TIMEOUT_EN_BIT   (1 << 7)
77	#define DCACHE_CACHE_BYPASS_BIT     (1 << 6)
78	
79	/* DCACHE_CACHE_STATUS bit fields */
80	
81	#define DCACHE_INIT_FINISH_BIT      (1 << 0)
82	
83	/* HPMCU clock rates (informational, used by rv1126b_clockconfig.c) */
84	
85	#define GPLL_RATE_HZ            1188000000u
86	#define HPMCU_RATE_HZ           396000000u
87	
88	#define RV1126B_DIAG_SKIP_DCACHE   1
89	#define RV1126B_DIAG_POLL_TIMEOUT  1000000

93	 ****************************************************************************/

95	extern uint32_t _sbss;     /* Start of BSS section */
96	extern uint32_t _ebss;     /* End of BSS section */
97	extern uint32_t _sdata;    /* Start of data section (in RAM) */
98	extern uint32_t _edata;    /* End of data section (in RAM) */
99	extern uint32_t _eronly;   /* Load address of data section (in ROM/flash) */

102	 * Private Functions
103	 ****************************************************************************/
104	
105	/****************************************************************************
106	 * Name: rv1126b_bss_init
107	 *
108	 * Description:
109	 *   Zero-fill the BSS section from _sbss to _ebss.
110	 *
111	 ****************************************************************************/
112	
113	static void rv1126b_bss_init(void)
114	{
115	  uint32_t *dest = &_sbss;
116	
117	  while (dest < &_ebss)
118	    {
119	      *dest++ = 0;
120	    }
121	}
122	
123	/****************************************************************************
124	 * Name: rv1126b_data_init
125	 *
126	 * Description:
127	 *   Copy initialized data from ROM/flash load address (_eronly) to RAM
128	 *   (_sdata.._edata).  If the data section is loaded directly into RAM
129	 *   (e.g., XIP from flash with data in-place), this is a no-op.
130	 *
131	 ****************************************************************************/
132	
133	static void rv1126b_data_init(void)
134	{
135	  uint32_t *src  = &_eronly;
136	  uint32_t *dest = &_sdata;
137	
138	  while (dest < &_edata)
139	    {
140	      *dest++ = *src++;
141	    }
142	}

144	/****************************************************************************
145	 * Name: rv1126b_dcache_init
146	 *
147	 * Description:
148	 *   Initialize the HPMCU DCache:
149	 *   - Configure the uncache address region via GRF_SYS so that
150	 *     memory-mapped peripherals (0x20000..0x23000) bypass the cache.
151	 *   - Enable DCache with store buffer (stb_entry=7, timeout enabled).
152	 *   - Wait for cache initialization to complete.
153	 *   - Clear the cache bypass bit to enable caching.
154	 *
155	 *   Note: Do not access uninitialized global variables before this
156	 *   function completes, as BSS must already be zeroed.
157	 *
158	 ****************************************************************************/
159	
160	static bool rv1126b_dcache_init(void)
161	{
162	  volatile uint32_t *grf_cache_start =
163	    (volatile uint32_t *)GRF_HPMCU_CACHE_ADDR_START;
164	  volatile uint32_t *grf_cache_end =
165	    (volatile uint32_t *)GRF_HPMCU_CACHE_ADDR_END;
166	  volatile uint32_t *dcache_ctrl =
167	    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_CACHE_CTRL;
168	  volatile uint32_t *dcache_status =
169	    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_CACHE_STATUS;
170	  volatile uint32_t *dcache_stb =
171	    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_STB_TIMEOUT_CTRL;
172	  volatile uint32_t timeout = RV1126B_DIAG_POLL_TIMEOUT;
173	
174	  /* Set the uncache region to cover peripheral address space */
175	
176	  *grf_cache_start = 0x20000;
177	  *grf_cache_end   = 0x23000;
178	
179	  /* Enable DCache: cache_en=1, stb_entry=7, stb_timeout_en=1 */
180	
181	  *dcache_ctrl |= DCACHE_CACHE_EN_BIT |
182	                  DCACHE_CACHE_ENTRY_THRESH |
183	                  DCACHE_STB_TIMEOUT_EN_BIT;
184	
185	  /* Enable store buffer timeout */
186	
187	  *dcache_stb = 1;
188	
189	  /* Wait for cache initialization to finish */
190	
191	  while ((*dcache_status & DCACHE_INIT_FINISH_BIT) == 0)
192	    {
193	      if (timeout-- == 0)
194	        {
195	          return false;
196	        }
197	    }
198	
199	  /* Clear bypass to enable caching */
200	
201	  *dcache_ctrl &= ~DCACHE_CACHE_BYPASS_BIT;
202	  return true;
203	}

92	      return 0;

23	/****************************************************************************
24	 * RV1126B HPMCU IRQ dispatch for NuttX
25	 *
26	 * This file implements the RISC-V interrupt dispatch logic for the
27	 * RV1126B HPMCU.  The SCR1 core uses the IPIC (CSR 0xbf0..0xbf7) for
28	 * interrupt prioritization and EOI/SOI handshaking, and the INTMUX
29	 * for external interrupt routing.
30	 *
31	 * Dispatch flow:
32	 *   1. Trap entry (rv1126b_head.S g_traps) saves context and calls
33	 *      riscv_dispatch_irq(mcause, regs).
34	 *   2. riscv_dispatch_irq() identifies the interrupt type and:
35	 *      - For timer interrupts (mcause=7): calls up_timer_int()
36	 *        and returns regs.
37	 *      - For external interrupts (mcause=11): scans INTMUX status
38	 *        registers to find the active IRQs, then dispatches each
39	 *        via riscv_doirq(irq, regs) (which handles context switch
40	 *        bookkeeping), wrapped by IPIC SOI/EOI.
41	 *   3. The returned regs pointer is used by the assembly trap exit
42	 *      to restore the (possibly switched) context.

113	 *
114	 * Description:
115	 *   Scan the INTMUX status registers to find the highest-priority
116	 *   active (pending and enabled) IRQ.
117	 *
118	 * Returned Value:
119	 *   IRQ number (0..255), or -1 if no active IRQ is found.
120	 *

122	
123	static int rv1126b_get_active_irq(void)
124	{
125	  int i;
126	  unsigned int status;
127	
128	  for (i = 0; i < INTMUX_NGROUPS; i++)
129	    {
130	      status = getreg32(RV1126B_INTMUX_BASE +
131	                         RV1126B_INTMUX_STATUS_OFFSET +
132	                         (i * RV1126B_INTMUX_GROUP_STRIDE));
133	      if (status != 0)
134	        {
135	          /* Find the lowest-numbered (highest priority) set bit */
136	
137	          int bit = __builtin_ctz(status);
138	          return i * INTMUX_IRQS_PER_GROUP + bit;
139	        }
140	    }
141	
142	  return -1;
143	}

149	/****************************************************************************
150	 * Name: riscv_dispatch_irq
151	 *
152	 * Description:
153	 *   Dispatch an interrupt based on the mcause value.
154	 *
155	 *   This function is called from the NuttX RISC-V common interrupt
156	 *   handling path (riscv_doirq -> riscv_dispatch_irq) when the mcause
157	 *   indicates an interrupt (bit 31 set).
158	 *
159	 *   For the RV1126B HPMCU:
160	 *     - mcause == 7  (IRQ_M_TIMER): machine timer interrupt
161	 *     - mcause == 11 (IRQ_M_EXT):   machine external interrupt
162	 *       (routed through INTMUX)
163	 *
164	 * Input Parameters:
165	 *   mcause - The value of the mcause CSR
166	 *   regs   - Pointer to the saved register context
167	 *
168	 * Returned Value:
169	 *   Pointer to the (possibly new) register context after dispatch.
170	 *
171	 ****************************************************************************/
172	
173	void *riscv_dispatch_irq(uintptr_t mcause, uintreg_t *regs)
174	{
175	  uintptr_t cause;
176	
177	  if ((mcause & MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT) == 0)
178	    {
179	      /* Synchronous exceptions must go through riscv_doirq() so NuttX can
180	       * advance mepc for ecall and handle context switching properly.
181	       */
182	
183	      regs = riscv_doirq((int)mcause, regs);
184	      return regs;
185	    }
186	
187	  /* Interrupt: strip the interrupt bit to get the cause code */
188	
189	  cause = mcause & ~MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT;
190	
191	  if (cause == IRQ_M_TIMER)
192	    {
193	      /* Machine timer interrupt -- call the NuttX timer handler */
194	
195	      up_timer_int();
196	    }
197	  else if (cause == IRQ_M_EXT)
198	    {
199	      /* Machine external interrupt -- scan INTMUX for active IRQs */
200	
201	      int irq;
202	
203	      /* Signal IPIC Start of Interrupt */
204	
205	      rv1126b_ipic_soi();
206	
207	      /* Scan for active IRQs -- handle all pending IRQs in this group */
208	
209	      while ((irq = rv1126b_get_active_irq()) >= 0)
210	        {
211	          /* Dispatch through the NuttX IRQ dispatch table.
212	           * riscv_doirq() handles context switch bookkeeping and
213	           * returns the (possibly updated) regs pointer.
214	           */
215	
216	          regs = riscv_doirq(irq, regs);
217	        }
218	
219	      /* Signal IPIC End of Interrupt */
220	
221	      rv1126b_ipic_eoi();
222	    }
223	  else
224	    {
225	      /* Unexpected interrupt cause -- spin */
226	
227	      for (; ; );
228	    }
229	
230	  return regs;
231	}

23	/****************************************************************************
24	 * RV1126B HPMCU IRQ dispatch for NuttX
25	 *
26	 * This file implements the RISC-V interrupt dispatch logic for the
27	 * RV1126B HPMCU.  The SCR1 core uses the IPIC (CSR 0xbf0..0xbf7) for
28	 * interrupt prioritization and EOI/SOI handshaking, and the INTMUX
29	 * for external interrupt routing.
30	 *
31	 * Dispatch flow:
32	 *   1. Trap entry (rv1126b_head.S g_traps) saves context and calls
33	 *      riscv_dispatch_irq(mcause, regs).
34	 *   2. riscv_dispatch_irq() identifies the interrupt type and:
35	 *      - For timer interrupts (mcause=7): calls up_timer_int()
36	 *        and returns regs.
37	 *      - For external interrupts (mcause=11): scans INTMUX status
38	 *        registers to find the active IRQs, then dispatches each
39	 *        via riscv_doirq(irq, regs) (which handles context switch
40	 *        bookkeeping), wrapped by IPIC SOI/EOI.
41	 *   3. The returned regs pointer is used by the assembly trap exit
42	 *      to restore the (possibly switched) context.
43	 ****************************************************************************/

112	 * Name: rv1126b_get_active_irq
113	 *
114	 * Description:
115	 *   Scan the INTMUX status registers to find the highest-priority
116	 *   active (pending and enabled) IRQ.
117	 *
118	 * Returned Value:
119	 *   IRQ number (0..255), or -1 if no active IRQ is found.
120	 *

122	
123	static int rv1126b_get_active_irq(void)
124	{
125	  int i;
126	  unsigned int status;
127	
128	  for (i = 0; i < INTMUX_NGROUPS; i++)
129	    {
130	      status = getreg32(RV1126B_INTMUX_BASE +
131	                         RV1126B_INTMUX_STATUS_OFFSET +
132	                         (i * RV1126B_INTMUX_GROUP_STRIDE));
133	      if (status != 0)
134	        {
135	          /* Find the lowest-numbered (highest priority) set bit */
136	
137	          int bit = __builtin_ctz(status);
138	          return i * INTMUX_IRQS_PER_GROUP + bit;
139	        }
140	    }
141	
142	  return -1;
143	}

149	/****************************************************************************
150	 * Name: riscv_dispatch_irq
151	 *
152	 * Description:
153	 *   Dispatch an interrupt based on the mcause value.
154	 *
155	 *   This function is called from the NuttX RISC-V common interrupt
156	 *   handling path (riscv_doirq -> riscv_dispatch_irq) when the mcause
157	 *   indicates an interrupt (bit 31 set).
158	 *
159	 *   For the RV1126B HPMCU:
160	 *     - mcause == 7  (IRQ_M_TIMER): machine timer interrupt
161	 *     - mcause == 11 (IRQ_M_EXT):   machine external interrupt
162	 *       (routed through INTMUX)
163	 *
164	 * Input Parameters:
165	 *   mcause - The value of the mcause CSR
166	 *   regs   - Pointer to the saved register context
167	 *
168	 * Returned Value:
169	 *   Pointer to the (possibly new) register context after dispatch.
170	 *
171	 ****************************************************************************/
172	
173	void *riscv_dispatch_irq(uintptr_t mcause, uintreg_t *regs)
174	{
175	  uintptr_t cause;
176	
177	  if ((mcause & MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT) == 0)
178	    {
179	      /* Synchronous exceptions must go through riscv_doirq() so NuttX can
180	       * advance mepc for ecall and handle context switching properly.
181	       */
182	
183	      regs = riscv_doirq((int)mcause, regs);
184	      return regs;
185	    }
186	
187	  /* Interrupt: strip the interrupt bit to get the cause code */
188	
189	  cause = mcause & ~MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT;
190	
191	  if (cause == IRQ_M_TIMER)
192	    {
193	      /* Machine timer interrupt -- call the NuttX timer handler */
194	
195	      up_timer_int();
196	    }
197	  else if (cause == IRQ_M_EXT)
198	    {
199	      /* Machine external interrupt -- scan INTMUX for active IRQs */
200	
201	      int irq;
202	
203	      /* Signal IPIC Start of Interrupt */
204	
205	      rv1126b_ipic_soi();
206	
207	      /* Scan for active IRQs -- handle all pending IRQs in this group */
208	
209	      while ((irq = rv1126b_get_active_irq()) >= 0)
210	        {
211	          /* Dispatch through the NuttX IRQ dispatch table.
212	           * riscv_doirq() handles context switch bookkeeping and
213	           * returns the (possibly updated) regs pointer.
214	           */
215	
216	          regs = riscv_doirq(irq, regs);
217	        }
218	
219	      /* Signal IPIC End of Interrupt */
220	
221	      rv1126b_ipic_eoi();
222	    }
223	  else
224	    {
225	      /* Unexpected interrupt cause -- spin */
226	
227	      for (; ; );
228	    }
229	
230	  return regs;
231	}

109	static void rv1126b_uart5_enable_clock(void)
110	{
111	  /* Select 24 MHz oscillator as UART5 source clock.
112	   * CLKSEL_CON14 at TOPCRU + 0x338:
113	   *   Bits [15:13] = SCLK_UART5_SRC_SEL (0 = XIN_OSC0 / 24 MHz)
114	   *   Bits [12:8]  = SCLK_UART5_SRC_DIV (0 = divide by 1)
115	   * Use Rockchip high-word write-mask semantics so unrelated fields are not
116	   * affected.
117	   */
118	
119	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE((0x7u << 13) | (0x1fu << 8), 0),
120	           TOPCRU_BASE + 0x338);
121	
122	  /* Enable UART5 source clock gate (SCLK_UART5_SRC_GATE in GATE_CON01)
123	   * Bit 14 of GATE_CON01 at TOPCRU + 0x804.
124	   * Gate bits are active-high disables, so write data 0 to enable.
125	   */
126	
127	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE(RV1126B_SCLK_UART5_SRC_GATE, 0),
128	           CONSOLE_SCLK_GATE_REG);
129	
130	  /* Enable UART5 peripheral clock gate (PCLK_UART5_GATE in GATE_CON04)
131	   * Bit 13 of GATE_CON04 at BUSCRU + 0x810.
132	   */
133	
134	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE(RV1126B_PCLK_UART5_GATE, 0),
135	           CONSOLE_PCLK_GATE_REG);
136	}

161	 *
162	 * Description:
163	 *   Configure GPIO4_A6 (TX) and GPIO4_A7 (RX) pin mux for UART5 M0
164	 *   function.  The IOC (I/O Controller) registers select the pin function.
165	 *
166	 *   SDK-verified mapping: UART5 M0 -> GPIO4_PA6 FUNC5, GPIO4_PA7 FUNC5.
167	 *
168	 ****************************************************************************/
169	
170	static void rv1126b_uart5_config_pins(void)
171	{
172	  /* GPIO4_A6 = UART5_TXM0 (FUNC5)
173	   * GPIO4_A7 = UART5_RXM0 (FUNC5)
174	   *
175	   * Both pins share GPIO4A_IOMUX_SEL_1 at GPIO4_IOC_BASE + 0x84:
176	   *   Bits [11:8]  = GPIO4_A6 function select (5 = UART5)
177	   *   Bits [15:12] = GPIO4_A7 function select (5 = UART5)
178	   *
179	   * SDK-verified: rv1126b.h GPIO4A6_SEL_SHIFT=8, GPIO4A7_SEL_SHIFT=12
180	   * Linux DTS: <4 RK_PA7 5 &pcfg_pull_up>, <4 RK_PA6 5 &pcfg_pull_up>
181	   * High-word masked write value: 0xff005500.
182	   */
183	
184	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE((0xfu << 8) | (0xfu << 12),
185	                                 (5u << 8) | (5u << 12)),
186	           GPIO4_IOC_BASE + 0x84);  /* GPIO4A_IOMUX_SEL_1 */
187	
188	  /* Enable pull-up on UART5 TX (GPIO4_PA6) and RX (GPIO4_PA7) pins
189	   * to prevent spurious characters when line is undriven.
190	   * GPIO4A_PULL at GPIO4_IOC_BASE + 0x340:
191	   *   bits [13:12] = GPIO4_A6 pull (1 = pull-up)
192	   *   bits [15:14] = GPIO4_A7 pull (1 = pull-up)
193	   * SDK/HAL-confirmed combined high-word write value: 0xf0005000.
194	   */
195	
196	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE((0x3u << 12) | (0x3u << 14),
197	                                 (1u << 12) | (1u << 14)),
198	           GPIO4_IOC_BASE + 0x340);  /* GPIO4A_PULL */
199	}

235	  putreg32((CONSOLE_DIVISOR >> 8) & 0xff, UART_DLH(UART_BASE));

238

109	static void rv1126b_uart5_enable_clock(void)
110	{
111	  /* Select 24 MHz oscillator as UART5 source clock.
112	   * CLKSEL_CON14 at TOPCRU + 0x338:
113	   *   Bits [15:13] = SCLK_UART5_SRC_SEL (0 = XIN_OSC0 / 24 MHz)
114	   *   Bits [12:8]  = SCLK_UART5_SRC_DIV (0 = divide by 1)
115	   * Use Rockchip high-word write-mask semantics so unrelated fields are not
116	   * affected.
117	   */
118	
119	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE((0x7u << 13) | (0x1fu << 8), 0),
120	           TOPCRU_BASE + 0x338);
121	
122	  /* Enable UART5 source clock gate (SCLK_UART5_SRC_GATE in GATE_CON01)
123	   * Bit 14 of GATE_CON01 at TOPCRU + 0x804.
124	   * Gate bits are active-high disables, so write data 0 to enable.
125	   */
126	
127	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE(RV1126B_SCLK_UART5_SRC_GATE, 0),
128	           CONSOLE_SCLK_GATE_REG);
129	
130	  /* Enable UART5 peripheral clock gate (PCLK_UART5_GATE in GATE_CON04)
131	   * Bit 13 of GATE_CON04 at BUSCRU + 0x810.
132	   */
133	
134	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE(RV1126B_PCLK_UART5_GATE, 0),
135	           CONSOLE_PCLK_GATE_REG);
136	}

160	 * Name: rv1126b_uart5_config_pins
161	 *
162	 * Description:
163	 *   Configure GPIO4_A6 (TX) and GPIO4_A7 (RX) pin mux for UART5 M0
164	 *   function.  The IOC (I/O Controller) registers select the pin function.
165	 *
166	 *   SDK-verified mapping: UART5 M0 -> GPIO4_PA6 FUNC5, GPIO4_PA7 FUNC5.
167	 *
168	 ****************************************************************************/
169	
170	static void rv1126b_uart5_config_pins(void)
171	{
172	  /* GPIO4_A6 = UART5_TXM0 (FUNC5)
173	   * GPIO4_A7 = UART5_RXM0 (FUNC5)
174	   *
175	   * Both pins share GPIO4A_IOMUX_SEL_1 at GPIO4_IOC_BASE + 0x84:
176	   *   Bits [11:8]  = GPIO4_A6 function select (5 = UART5)
177	   *   Bits [15:12] = GPIO4_A7 function select (5 = UART5)
178	   *
179	   * SDK-verified: rv1126b.h GPIO4A6_SEL_SHIFT=8, GPIO4A7_SEL_SHIFT=12
180	   * Linux DTS: <4 RK_PA7 5 &pcfg_pull_up>, <4 RK_PA6 5 &pcfg_pull_up>
181	   * High-word masked write value: 0xff005500.
182	   */
183	
184	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE((0xfu << 8) | (0xfu << 12),
185	                                 (5u << 8) | (5u << 12)),
186	           GPIO4_IOC_BASE + 0x84);  /* GPIO4A_IOMUX_SEL_1 */
187	
188	  /* Enable pull-up on UART5 TX (GPIO4_PA6) and RX (GPIO4_PA7) pins
189	   * to prevent spurious characters when line is undriven.
190	   * GPIO4A_PULL at GPIO4_IOC_BASE + 0x340:
191	   *   bits [13:12] = GPIO4_A6 pull (1 = pull-up)
192	   *   bits [15:14] = GPIO4_A7 pull (1 = pull-up)
193	   * SDK/HAL-confirmed combined high-word write value: 0xf0005000.
194	   */
195	
196	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE((0x3u << 12) | (0x3u << 14),
197	                                 (1u << 12) | (1u << 14)),
198	           GPIO4_IOC_BASE + 0x340);  /* GPIO4A_PULL */
199	}

209	
210	static void rv1126b_uart5_init_hw(void)
211	{
212	  /* Software reset UART5 */
213	
214	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_SRR_UR | RV1126B_UART_SRR_RFR |
215	           RV1126B_UART_SRR_XFR, UART_SRR(UART_BASE));
216	
217	  /* Disable all interrupts */
218	
219	  putreg32(0, UART_IER(UART_BASE));
220	
221	  /* Enable FIFO, reset TX and RX FIFOs */
222	
223	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_FCR_FIFOE | RV1126B_UART_FCR_RFIFOR |
224	           RV1126B_UART_FCR_XFIFOR, UART_FCR(UART_BASE));
225	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_FCR_FIFOE | RV1126B_UART_FCR_TFT_TWO |
226	           RV1126B_UART_FCR_RT_HALF, UART_FCR(UART_BASE));
227	
228	  /* Set baud rate: enable DLAB, write divisor, disable DLAB
229	   * Divisor is computed from CONSOLE_CLK_RATE and CONSOLE_BAUD_RATE
230	   * in rv1126b_config.h (Kconfig-derived, default 1500000 baud).
231	   */
232	
233	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_LCR_DLAB, UART_LCR(UART_BASE));
234	  putreg32(CONSOLE_DIVISOR & 0xff, UART_DLL(UART_BASE));
235	  putreg32((CONSOLE_DIVISOR >> 8) & 0xff, UART_DLH(UART_BASE));
236	
237	  /* Set line control: 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit (8N1) */
238	
239	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_LCR_DLS_8 | RV1126B_UART_LCR_STOP_1,
240	           UART_LCR(UART_BASE));
241	}

179	/****************************************************************************
180	 * Name: rv1126b_uart_setup
181	 *
182	 * Description:
183	 *   Configure the UART for the current baud rate and format.
184	 *   Enable the UART clock and configure pins if not already done.
185	 *
186	 ****************************************************************************/
187	
188	static int rv1126b_uart_setup(struct uart_dev_s *dev)
189	{
190	  struct rv1126b_uart_s *priv = (struct rv1126b_uart_s *)dev->priv;
191	  uint32_t base = priv->base;
192	  uint32_t divisor;
193	  irqstate_t flags;
194	
195	  flags = enter_critical_section();
196	
197	  /* Software reset the UART */
198	
199	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_SRR_UR | RV1126B_UART_SRR_RFR |
200	           RV1126B_UART_SRR_XFR, UART_SRR(base));
201	
202	  /* Disable all interrupts */
203	
204	  putreg32(0, UART_IER(base));
205	
206	  /* Enable FIFO, reset TX and RX FIFOs */
207	
208	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_FCR_FIFOE | RV1126B_UART_FCR_RFIFOR |
209	           RV1126B_UART_FCR_XFIFOR, UART_FCR(base));
210	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_FCR_FIFOE | RV1126B_UART_FCR_TFT_TWO |
211	           RV1126B_UART_FCR_RT_HALF, UART_FCR(base));
212	
213	  /* Set baud rate */
214	
215	  divisor = priv->clk_rate / 16 / priv->baud;
216	
217	  /* Enable DLAB to access divisor latch registers */
218	
219	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_LCR_DLAB, UART_LCR(base));
220	  putreg32(divisor & 0xff, UART_DLL(base));
221	  putreg32((divisor >> 8) & 0xff, UART_DLH(base));
222	
223	  /* Set line control: 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit (8N1) */
224	
225	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_LCR_DLS_8 | RV1126B_UART_LCR_STOP_1,
226	           UART_LCR(base));
227	
228	  leave_critical_section(flags);
229	
230	  return OK;
231	}

181	 *
182	 * Description:
183	 *   Configure the UART for the current baud rate and format.
184	 *   Enable the UART clock and configure pins if not already done.

186	 ****************************************************************************/
187	
188	static int rv1126b_uart_setup(struct uart_dev_s *dev)
189	{
190	  struct rv1126b_uart_s *priv = (struct rv1126b_uart_s *)dev->priv;
191	  uint32_t base = priv->base;
192	  uint32_t divisor;
193	  irqstate_t flags;
194	
195	  flags = enter_critical_section();
196	
197	  /* Software reset the UART */
198	
199	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_SRR_UR | RV1126B_UART_SRR_RFR |
200	           RV1126B_UART_SRR_XFR, UART_SRR(base));
201	
202	  /* Disable all interrupts */
203	
204	  putreg32(0, UART_IER(base));
205	
206	  /* Enable FIFO, reset TX and RX FIFOs */
207	
208	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_FCR_FIFOE | RV1126B_UART_FCR_RFIFOR |
209	           RV1126B_UART_FCR_XFIFOR, UART_FCR(base));
210	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_FCR_FIFOE | RV1126B_UART_FCR_TFT_TWO |
211	           RV1126B_UART_FCR_RT_HALF, UART_FCR(base));
212	
213	  /* Set baud rate */
214	
215	  divisor = priv->clk_rate / 16 / priv->baud;
216	
217	  /* Enable DLAB to access divisor latch registers */
218	
219	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_LCR_DLAB, UART_LCR(base));
220	  putreg32(divisor & 0xff, UART_DLL(base));
221	  putreg32((divisor >> 8) & 0xff, UART_DLH(base));
222	
223	  /* Set line control: 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit (8N1) */
224	
225	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_LCR_DLS_8 | RV1126B_UART_LCR_STOP_1,
226	           UART_LCR(base));
227	
228	  leave_critical_section(flags);
229	
230	  return OK;
231	}

/****************************************************************************
 * RV1126B HPMCU interrupt controller (INTMUX) for NuttX
 *
 * The RV1126B HPMCU uses a RISC-V SCR1 core with a local interrupt
 * controller (IPIC) and an external interrupt multiplexer (INTMUX).
 * External interrupts from peripherals are routed through the INTMUX
 * before reaching the machine external interrupt (MEIP) line.
 *
 * INTMUX register layout:
 *   Base: 0x20b40000
 *   Enable registers: offset 0x00..0x1C (8 groups x 32 bits = 256 IRQs)
 *   Status registers: offset 0x80..0x9C (8 groups x 32 bits)
 *
 * The IPIC (CSR 0xbf0..0xbf7) is used for EOI/SOI handshaking with the
 * SCR1 interrupt controller.
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Included Files
 ****************************************************************************/

#include <nuttx/config.h>
#include <nuttx/irq.h>
#include <nuttx/arch.h>

#include <stdint.h>

#include "riscv_internal.h"
#include "chip.h"

/****************************************************************************
 * Pre-processor Definitions
 ****************************************************************************/

/* INTMUX definitions from hardware/rv1126b_intmux.h */

#define INTMUX_NGROUPS          RV1126B_INTMUX_NGROUPS  /* 8 groups */
#define INTMUX_IRQS_PER_GROUP   32
#define INTMUX_NR_IRQS          (INTMUX_NGROUPS * INTMUX_IRQS_PER_GROUP)

/****************************************************************************
 * Private Data
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Private Functions
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: rv1126b_intmux_enable
 *
 * Description:
 *   Enable a specific IRQ in the INTMUX enable registers.
 *   Uses the RV1126B_INTMUX_ENABLE(n) macro from rv1126b_intmux.h.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   irq - IRQ number (0..255)
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

static void rv1126b_intmux_enable(int irq)
{
  uintptr_t reg = RV1126B_INTMUX_ENABLE(irq);
  unsigned int bit = irq % INTMUX_IRQS_PER_GROUP;

  putreg32(getreg32(reg) | (1u << bit), reg);
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: rv1126b_intmux_disable
 *
 * Description:
 *   Disable a specific IRQ in the INTMUX enable registers.
 *   Uses the RV1126B_INTMUX_ENABLE(n) macro from rv1126b_intmux.h.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   irq - IRQ number (0..255)
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

static void rv1126b_intmux_disable(int irq)
{
  uintptr_t reg = RV1126B_INTMUX_ENABLE(irq);
  unsigned int bit = irq % INTMUX_IRQS_PER_GROUP;

  putreg32(getreg32(reg) & ~(1u << bit), reg);
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Functions
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: up_irqinitialize
 *
 * Description:
 *   Initialize the interrupt subsystem for the RV1126B HPMCU.
 *   - Disable all INTMUX enables
 *   - Set mtvec to the trap vector
 *   - Enable machine external interrupts in MIE
 *   - Enable global interrupts
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

void up_irqinitialize(void)
{
  int i;

  /* Disable all INTMUX interrupt enables */

  for (i = 0; i < INTMUX_NGROUPS; i++)
    {
      putreg32(0, RV1126B_INTMUX_BASE + RV1126B_INTMUX_ENABLE_OFFSET +
                (i * RV1126B_INTMUX_GROUP_STRIDE));
    }

  /* Enable all IPIC vectors before enabling MEIP.  write_csr() stringifies
   * its CSR argument, so these CSR numbers must remain literals.
   */

  for (i = 0; i < 16; i++)
    {
      write_csr(0xbf6, i);
      write_csr(0xbf7, 1u << 1);
    }

  /* Note: mtvec is already set to the NuttX trap vector
   * (g_traps in rv1126b_head.S) before NuttX code runs.
   */

  /* Enable machine external interrupts (MEIP) in the mie CSR */

  set_csr(mie, MIP_MEIP);

  /* Enable global interrupts */

  up_irq_enable();
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: up_enable_irq
 *
 * Description:
 *   Enable the specified IRQ in the INTMUX.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   irq - IRQ number to enable
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

void up_enable_irq(int irq)
{
  rv1126b_intmux_enable(irq);
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: up_disable_irq
 *
 * Description:
 *   Disable the specified IRQ in the INTMUX.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   irq - IRQ number to disable
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

void up_disable_irq(int irq)
{
  rv1126b_intmux_disable(irq);
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: up_irq_enable
 *
 * Description:
 *   Enable interrupts and return the previous interrupt state.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

irqstate_t up_irq_enable(void)
{
  irqstate_t flags;

  __asm__ __volatile__
    (
      "csrrs %0, mstatus, %1\n"
      : "=r" (flags)
      : "r"(MSTATUS_MIE)
      : "memory"
    );

  return flags;
}

#include "hardware/rv1126b_timer.h"
#include "hardware/rv1126b_uart.h"

/****************************************************************************
 * RISC-V CSR Helper Macros
 *
 * These are needed for inline CSR access in C code (set_csr, clear_csr,
 * read_csr, write_csr).  They follow the same pattern as the SDK
 * riscv_csr_encoding.h.
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifndef __ASSEMBLY__

#ifdef __GNUC__

#define read_csr(reg) \
  ({ unsigned long __tmp; \
     asm volatile ("csrr %0, " #reg : "=r"(__tmp)); \
     __tmp; })

#define write_csr(reg, val) \
  ({ asm volatile ("csrw " #reg ", %0" :: "rK"(val)); })

#define set_csr(reg, bit) \
  ({ unsigned long __tmp; \
     asm volatile ("csrrs %0, " #reg ", %1" : "=r"(__tmp) : "rK"(bit)); \
     __tmp; })

#define clear_csr(reg, bit) \
  ({ unsigned long __tmp; \
     asm volatile ("csrrc %0, " #reg ", %1" : "=r"(__tmp) : "rK"(bit)); \
     __tmp; })

#endif /* __GNUC__ */

/****************************************************************************
 * MSTATUS and MIP bit definitions
 *
 * These supplement the CSR macros for interrupt control.
 ****************************************************************************/

#define MSTATUS_MIE     0x00000008
#define MIP_MEIP        0x00000800  /* Machine external interrupt pending */
#define MIP_MTIP        0x00000080  /* Machine timer interrupt pending */
#define MIP_MSIP        0x00000008  /* Machine software interrupt pending */

/****************************************************************************
 * RISC-V Interrupt Cause Codes
 ****************************************************************************/

#define IRQ_M_SOFT      3
#define IRQ_M_TIMER     7
#define IRQ_M_EXT       11

void rv1126b_clockconfig(void); /* Clock config from rv1126b_clockconfig.c */

#endif /* !__ASSEMBLY__ */

61	backtrace_helper(FAR struct _Unwind_Context *ctx, FAR void *a)
62	{
63	  FAR struct trace_arg *arg = a;
64	
65	  /* We are first called with address in the backtrace function.
66	   * Skip it.
67	   */
68	
69	  if (arg->cnt >= 0)
70	    {
71	      arg->array[arg->cnt] = (FAR void *)_Unwind_GetIP(ctx);
72	      if (arg->cnt > 0)
73	        {
74	          arg->array[arg->cnt]
75	            = unwind_arch_adjustment(arg->array[arg->cnt - 1],
76	                arg->array[arg->cnt]);
77	        }
78	
79	      /* Check whether we make any progress. */
80	
81	      _Unwind_Word cfa = _Unwind_GetCFA(ctx);
82	
83	      if (arg->cnt > 0 &&
84	          arg->array[arg->cnt - 1] == arg->array[arg->cnt] &&
85	          cfa == arg->cfa)
86	        {
87	          return _URC_END_OF_STACK;
88	        }
89	
90	      arg->cfa = cfa;
91	    }
92	
93	  if (++arg->cnt >= arg->size)
94	    {
95	      return _URC_END_OF_STACK;
96	    }
97	
98	  return _URC_NO_REASON;
99	}

116	
117	  if (tid != _SCHED_GETTID())
118	    {
119	      return 0;
120	    }
121	
122	  arg.array = buffer;
123	  arg.cfa = 0;
124	  arg.size = size;
125	  arg.cnt = -skip - 1;
126

`max effort → 5+5 angles × 8 candidates → 1-vote verify → sweep → ≤15 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at maximum effort: catch every real bug. At
this level, catching real bugs matters more than avoiding false positives — a
missed bug ships. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (5 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 8 each)

Run **10 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 8 candidate findings**. Do NOT let one angle's conclusions
suppress another's — if two angles flag the same line for different reasons,
record both.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Angle D — language-pitfall specialist

Scan for the classic pitfalls of the diff's language/framework — for example:
JS falsy-zero, `==` coercion, closure-captured loop var; Python mutable default
args, late-binding closures; Go nil-map write, range-var capture; SQL injection;
timezone/DST drift; float equality. Flag any instance the diff introduces.

### Angle E — wrapper/proxy correctness

When the PR adds or modifies a type that wraps another (cache, proxy, decorator,
adapter): check that every method routes to the wrapped instance and not back
through a registry/session/global — e.g. a caching provider holding a
`delegate` field that resolves IDs via `session.get(...)` instead of
`delegate.get(...)` will re-enter the cache or recurse. Also check that the
wrapper forwards all the methods the callers actually use.

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, 3-state)

Dedup candidates that point at the same line/mechanism, keeping the one with
the most concrete failure scenario. For each remaining candidate, run **one
verifier** via the Agent tool: give it the diff, the relevant
file(s), and the candidate, and have it return exactly one of:

- **CONFIRMED** — can name the inputs/state that trigger it and the wrong
  output or crash. Quote the line.
- **PLAUSIBLE** — mechanism is real, trigger is uncertain (timing, env,
  config). State what would confirm it.
- **REFUTED** — factually wrong (code doesn't say that) or guarded elsewhere.
  Quote the line that proves it.

Keep candidates where the vote is CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE.

This is recall mode — a single non-REFUTED vote carries the finding. Do NOT
drop on uncertainty.

## Phase 3 — Sweep for gaps

Run **one more finder** as a fresh reviewer who has the verified list. Re-read
the diff and enclosing functions looking ONLY for defects not already listed.
Do not re-derive or re-confirm anything already there — the job is gaps. Focus
on what the first pass tends to miss: moved/extracted code that dropped a guard
or anchor; second-tier footguns (dataclass default evaluated once, `hash()`
non-determinism, lock-scope shrink, predicate methods with side effects);
setup/teardown asymmetry in tests; config defaults flipped.

Surface **up to 8 additional candidates**, each naming a defect not already on
the list. If nothing new, return an empty sweep — do not pad.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 15 objects:

[

    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 15 survive, keep the 15 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`.

23	/****************************************************************************
24	 * RV1126B HPMCU IRQ dispatch for NuttX
25	 *
26	 * This file implements the RISC-V interrupt dispatch logic for the
27	 * RV1126B HPMCU.  The SCR1 core uses the IPIC (CSR 0xbf0..0xbf7) for
28	 * interrupt prioritization and EOI/SOI handshaking, and the INTMUX
29	 * for external interrupt routing.
30	 *
31	 * Dispatch flow:
32	 *   1. Trap entry (rv1126b_head.S g_traps) saves context and calls
33	 *      riscv_dispatch_irq(mcause, regs).
34	 *   2. riscv_dispatch_irq() identifies the interrupt type and:
35	 *      - For timer interrupts (mcause=7): calls up_timer_int()
36	 *        and returns regs.
37	 *      - For external interrupts (mcause=11): scans INTMUX status
38	 *        registers to find the active IRQs, then dispatches each
39	 *        via riscv_doirq(irq, regs) (which handles context switch
40	 *        bookkeeping), wrapped by IPIC SOI/EOI.
41	 *   3. The returned regs pointer is used by the assembly trap exit
42	 *      to restore the (possibly switched) context.
43	 ****************************************************************************/
44

89	 *
90	 ****************************************************************************/

92	static inline void rv1126b_ipic_soi(void)

95	}

99	 *

102	 *   interrupt processing.  Any value can be written.
103	 *
104	 ****************************************************************************/
105

107	{

109	}

111	/****************************************************************************
112	 * Name: rv1126b_get_active_irq
113	 *
114	 * Description:
115	 *   Scan the INTMUX status registers to find the highest-priority
116	 *   active (pending and enabled) IRQ.
117	 *
118	 * Returned Value:
119	 *   IRQ number (0..255), or -1 if no active IRQ is found.
120	 *
121	 ****************************************************************************/
122	
123	static int rv1126b_get_active_irq(void)
124	{
125	  int i;
126	  unsigned int status;
127	
128	  for (i = 0; i < INTMUX_NGROUPS; i++)
129	    {
130	      status = getreg32(RV1126B_INTMUX_BASE +
131	                         RV1126B_INTMUX_STATUS_OFFSET +
132	                         (i * RV1126B_INTMUX_GROUP_STRIDE));
133	      if (status != 0)
134	        {
135	          /* Find the lowest-numbered (highest priority) set bit */
136	
137	          int bit = __builtin_ctz(status);
138	          return i * INTMUX_IRQS_PER_GROUP + bit;
139	        }
140	    }
141	
142	  return -1;
143	}

149	/****************************************************************************
150	 * Name: riscv_dispatch_irq
151	 *
152	 * Description:
153	 *   Dispatch an interrupt based on the mcause value.
154	 *
155	 *   This function is called from the NuttX RISC-V common interrupt
156	 *   handling path (riscv_doirq -> riscv_dispatch_irq) when the mcause
157	 *   indicates an interrupt (bit 31 set).
158	 *
159	 *   For the RV1126B HPMCU:
160	 *     - mcause == 7  (IRQ_M_TIMER): machine timer interrupt
161	 *     - mcause == 11 (IRQ_M_EXT):   machine external interrupt
162	 *       (routed through INTMUX)
163	 *
164	 * Input Parameters:
165	 *   mcause - The value of the mcause CSR
166	 *   regs   - Pointer to the saved register context
167	 *
168	 * Returned Value:
169	 *   Pointer to the (possibly new) register context after dispatch.
170	 *
171	 ****************************************************************************/
172	
173	void *riscv_dispatch_irq(uintptr_t mcause, uintreg_t *regs)
174	{
175	  uintptr_t cause;
176	
177	  if ((mcause & MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT) == 0)
178	    {
179	      /* Synchronous exceptions must go through riscv_doirq() so NuttX can
180	       * advance mepc for ecall and handle context switching properly.
181	       */
182	
183	      regs = riscv_doirq((int)mcause, regs);
184	      return regs;
185	    }
186	
187	  /* Interrupt: strip the interrupt bit to get the cause code */
188	
189	  cause = mcause & ~MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT;
190	
191	  if (cause == IRQ_M_TIMER)
192	    {
193	      /* Machine timer interrupt -- call the NuttX timer handler */
194	
195	      up_timer_int();
196	    }
197	  else if (cause == IRQ_M_EXT)
198	    {
199	      /* Machine external interrupt -- scan INTMUX for active IRQs */
200	
201	      int irq;
202	
203	      /* Signal IPIC Start of Interrupt */
204	
205	      rv1126b_ipic_soi();
206	
207	      /* Scan for active IRQs -- handle all pending IRQs in this group */
208	
209	      while ((irq = rv1126b_get_active_irq()) >= 0)
210	        {
211	          /* Dispatch through the NuttX IRQ dispatch table.
212	           * riscv_doirq() handles context switch bookkeeping and
213	           * returns the (possibly updated) regs pointer.
214	           */
215	
216	          regs = riscv_doirq(irq, regs);
217	        }
218	
219	      /* Signal IPIC End of Interrupt */
220	
221	      rv1126b_ipic_eoi();
222	    }
223	  else
224	    {
225	      /* Unexpected interrupt cause -- spin */
226	
227	      for (; ; );
228	    }
229	
230	  return regs;
231	}

146	 *
147	 * Description:
148	 *   Initialize the HPMCU DCache:
149	 *   - Configure the uncache address region via GRF_SYS so that
150	 *     memory-mapped peripherals (0x20000..0x23000) bypass the cache.
151	 *   - Enable DCache with store buffer (stb_entry=7, timeout enabled).
152	 *   - Wait for cache initialization to complete.
153	 *   - Clear the cache bypass bit to enable caching.
154	 *
155	 *   Note: Do not access uninitialized global variables before this
156	 *   function completes, as BSS must already be zeroed.

160	static bool rv1126b_dcache_init(void)
161	{
162	  volatile uint32_t *grf_cache_start =
163	    (volatile uint32_t *)GRF_HPMCU_CACHE_ADDR_START;
164	  volatile uint32_t *grf_cache_end =
165	    (volatile uint32_t *)GRF_HPMCU_CACHE_ADDR_END;
166	  volatile uint32_t *dcache_ctrl =
167	    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_CACHE_CTRL;
168	  volatile uint32_t *dcache_status =
169	    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_CACHE_STATUS;
170	  volatile uint32_t *dcache_stb =
171	    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_STB_TIMEOUT_CTRL;
172	  volatile uint32_t timeout = RV1126B_DIAG_POLL_TIMEOUT;
173	
174	  /* Set the uncache region to cover peripheral address space */
175	
176	  *grf_cache_start = 0x20000;
177	  *grf_cache_end   = 0x23000;
178	
179	  /* Enable DCache: cache_en=1, stb_entry=7, stb_timeout_en=1 */
180	
181	  *dcache_ctrl |= DCACHE_CACHE_EN_BIT |
182	                  DCACHE_CACHE_ENTRY_THRESH |
183	                  DCACHE_STB_TIMEOUT_EN_BIT;
184	
185	  /* Enable store buffer timeout */
186	
187	  *dcache_stb = 1;
188	
189	  /* Wait for cache initialization to finish */
190	
191	  while ((*dcache_status & DCACHE_INIT_FINISH_BIT) == 0)
192	    {
193	      if (timeout-- == 0)
194	        {
195	          return false;
196	        }
197	    }
198	
199	  /* Clear bypass to enable caching */
200	
201	  *dcache_ctrl &= ~DCACHE_CACHE_BYPASS_BIT;
202	  return true;
203	}

23	/****************************************************************************
24	 * RV1126B HPMCU IRQ dispatch for NuttX
25	 *
26	 * This file implements the RISC-V interrupt dispatch logic for the
27	 * RV1126B HPMCU.  The SCR1 core uses the IPIC (CSR 0xbf0..0xbf7) for
28	 * interrupt prioritization and EOI/SOI handshaking, and the INTMUX
29	 * for external interrupt routing.
30	 *
31	 * Dispatch flow:
32	 *   1. Trap entry (rv1126b_head.S g_traps) saves context and calls
33	 *      riscv_dispatch_irq(mcause, regs).
34	 *   2. riscv_dispatch_irq() identifies the interrupt type and:
35	 *      - For timer interrupts (mcause=7): calls up_timer_int()
36	 *        and returns regs.
37	 *      - For external interrupts (mcause=11): scans INTMUX status
38	 *        registers to find the active IRQs, then dispatches each
39	 *        via riscv_doirq(irq, regs) (which handles context switch
40	 *        bookkeeping), wrapped by IPIC SOI/EOI.
41	 *   3. The returned regs pointer is used by the assembly trap exit
42	 *      to restore the (possibly switched) context.
43	 ****************************************************************************/

114	 * Description:
115	 *   Scan the INTMUX status registers to find the highest-priority
116	 *   active (pending and enabled) IRQ.
117	 *
118	 * Returned Value:
119	 *   IRQ number (0..255), or -1 if no active IRQ is found.
120	 *

123	static int rv1126b_get_active_irq(void)
124	{
125	  int i;
126	  unsigned int status;
127	
128	  for (i = 0; i < INTMUX_NGROUPS; i++)
129	    {
130	      status = getreg32(RV1126B_INTMUX_BASE +
131	                         RV1126B_INTMUX_STATUS_OFFSET +
132	                         (i * RV1126B_INTMUX_GROUP_STRIDE));
133	      if (status != 0)
134	        {
135	          /* Find the lowest-numbered (highest priority) set bit */
136	
137	          int bit = __builtin_ctz(status);
138	          return i * INTMUX_IRQS_PER_GROUP + bit;
139	        }
140	    }
141	
142	  return -1;

149	/****************************************************************************
150	 * Name: riscv_dispatch_irq
151	 *
152	 * Description:
153	 *   Dispatch an interrupt based on the mcause value.
154	 *
155	 *   This function is called from the NuttX RISC-V common interrupt
156	 *   handling path (riscv_doirq -> riscv_dispatch_irq) when the mcause
157	 *   indicates an interrupt (bit 31 set).
158	 *
159	 *   For the RV1126B HPMCU:
160	 *     - mcause == 7  (IRQ_M_TIMER): machine timer interrupt
161	 *     - mcause == 11 (IRQ_M_EXT):   machine external interrupt
162	 *       (routed through INTMUX)
163	 *
164	 * Input Parameters:
165	 *   mcause - The value of the mcause CSR
166	 *   regs   - Pointer to the saved register context
167	 *
168	 * Returned Value:
169	 *   Pointer to the (possibly new) register context after dispatch.
170	 *
171	 ****************************************************************************/
172	
173	void *riscv_dispatch_irq(uintptr_t mcause, uintreg_t *regs)
174	{
175	  uintptr_t cause;
176	
177	  if ((mcause & MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT) == 0)
178	    {
179	      /* Synchronous exceptions must go through riscv_doirq() so NuttX can
180	       * advance mepc for ecall and handle context switching properly.
181	       */
182	
183	      regs = riscv_doirq((int)mcause, regs);
184	      return regs;
185	    }
186	
187	  /* Interrupt: strip the interrupt bit to get the cause code */
188	
189	  cause = mcause & ~MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT;
190	
191	  if (cause == IRQ_M_TIMER)
192	    {
193	      /* Machine timer interrupt -- call the NuttX timer handler */
194	
195	      up_timer_int();
196	    }
197	  else if (cause == IRQ_M_EXT)
198	    {
199	      /* Machine external interrupt -- scan INTMUX for active IRQs */
200	
201	      int irq;
202	
203	      /* Signal IPIC Start of Interrupt */
204	
205	      rv1126b_ipic_soi();
206	
207	      /* Scan for active IRQs -- handle all pending IRQs in this group */
208	
209	      while ((irq = rv1126b_get_active_irq()) >= 0)
210	        {
211	          /* Dispatch through the NuttX IRQ dispatch table.
212	           * riscv_doirq() handles context switch bookkeeping and
213	           * returns the (possibly updated) regs pointer.
214	           */
215	
216	          regs = riscv_doirq(irq, regs);

218	
219	      /* Signal IPIC End of Interrupt */

221	      rv1126b_ipic_eoi();
222	    }
223	  else
224	    {
225	      /* Unexpected interrupt cause -- spin */
226	
227	      for (; ; );
228	    }
229	
230	  return regs;

51	 * Pre-processor Definitions
52	 ****************************************************************************/

54	/* GRF_SYS HPMCU cache address region registers.
55	 * These configure the uncache region for memory-mapped peripherals.
56	 * From RV1126B TRM: GRF_SYS at 0x20100000 (MCU view).
57	 */
58	
59	#define GRF_SYS_MCU_BASE            RV1126B_GRF_SYS_BASE
60	#define GRF_HPMCU_CACHE_ADDR_START  (GRF_SYS_MCU_BASE + 0x001C)
61	#define GRF_HPMCU_CACHE_ADDR_END    (GRF_SYS_MCU_BASE + 0x0020)
62	
63	/* DCACHE control registers.
64	 * From RV1126B memory map: DCACHE at 0x209D0000 (MCU view).
65	 */
66	
67	#define DCACHE_BASE                 RV1126B_DCACHE_BASE
68	#define DCACHE_CACHE_CTRL       (DCACHE_BASE + 0x0000)
69	#define DCACHE_CACHE_STATUS     (DCACHE_BASE + 0x0030)
70	#define DCACHE_STB_TIMEOUT_CTRL (DCACHE_BASE + 0x000C)
71	
72	/* DCACHE_CACHE_CTRL bit fields */
73	
74	#define DCACHE_CACHE_EN_BIT         (1 << 0)
75	#define DCACHE_CACHE_ENTRY_THRESH   (7 << 8)   /* stb_entry = 7 */
76	#define DCACHE_STB_TIMEOUT_EN_BIT   (1 << 7)
77	#define DCACHE_CACHE_BYPASS_BIT     (1 << 6)
78	
79	/* DCACHE_CACHE_STATUS bit fields */
80	
81	#define DCACHE_INIT_FINISH_BIT      (1 << 0)
82	
83	/* HPMCU clock rates (informational, used by rv1126b_clockconfig.c) */
84	
85	#define GPLL_RATE_HZ            1188000000u
86	#define HPMCU_RATE_HZ           396000000u
87	
88	#define RV1126B_DIAG_SKIP_DCACHE   1
89	#define RV1126B_DIAG_POLL_TIMEOUT  1000000

93	 ****************************************************************************/

95	extern uint32_t _sbss;     /* Start of BSS section */
96	extern uint32_t _ebss;     /* End of BSS section */
97	extern uint32_t _sdata;    /* Start of data section (in RAM) */
98	extern uint32_t _edata;    /* End of data section (in RAM) */
99	extern uint32_t _eronly;   /* Load address of data section (in ROM/flash) */

102	 * Private Functions
103	 ****************************************************************************/
104	
105	/****************************************************************************
106	 * Name: rv1126b_bss_init
107	 *
108	 * Description:
109	 *   Zero-fill the BSS section from _sbss to _ebss.
110	 *
111	 ****************************************************************************/
112	
113	static void rv1126b_bss_init(void)
114	{
115	  uint32_t *dest = &_sbss;
116	
117	  while (dest < &_ebss)
118	    {
119	      *dest++ = 0;
120	    }
121	}
122	
123	/****************************************************************************
124	 * Name: rv1126b_data_init
125	 *
126	 * Description:
127	 *   Copy initialized data from ROM/flash load address (_eronly) to RAM
128	 *   (_sdata.._edata).  If the data section is loaded directly into RAM
129	 *   (e.g., XIP from flash with data in-place), this is a no-op.
130	 *
131	 ****************************************************************************/
132	
133	static void rv1126b_data_init(void)
134	{
135	  uint32_t *src  = &_eronly;
136	  uint32_t *dest = &_sdata;
137	
138	  while (dest < &_edata)
139	    {
140	      *dest++ = *src++;
141	    }
142	}

144	/****************************************************************************
145	 * Name: rv1126b_dcache_init
146	 *
147	 * Description:
148	 *   Initialize the HPMCU DCache:
149	 *   - Configure the uncache address region via GRF_SYS so that
150	 *     memory-mapped peripherals (0x20000..0x23000) bypass the cache.
151	 *   - Enable DCache with store buffer (stb_entry=7, timeout enabled).
152	 *   - Wait for cache initialization to complete.
153	 *   - Clear the cache bypass bit to enable caching.
154	 *
155	 *   Note: Do not access uninitialized global variables before this
156	 *   function completes, as BSS must already be zeroed.
157	 *
158	 ****************************************************************************/
159	
160	static bool rv1126b_dcache_init(void)
161	{
162	  volatile uint32_t *grf_cache_start =
163	    (volatile uint32_t *)GRF_HPMCU_CACHE_ADDR_START;
164	  volatile uint32_t *grf_cache_end =
165	    (volatile uint32_t *)GRF_HPMCU_CACHE_ADDR_END;
166	  volatile uint32_t *dcache_ctrl =
167	    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_CACHE_CTRL;
168	  volatile uint32_t *dcache_status =
169	    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_CACHE_STATUS;
170	  volatile uint32_t *dcache_stb =
171	    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_STB_TIMEOUT_CTRL;
172	  volatile uint32_t timeout = RV1126B_DIAG_POLL_TIMEOUT;
173	
174	  /* Set the uncache region to cover peripheral address space */
175	
176	  *grf_cache_start = 0x20000;
177	  *grf_cache_end   = 0x23000;
178	
179	  /* Enable DCache: cache_en=1, stb_entry=7, stb_timeout_en=1 */
180	
181	  *dcache_ctrl |= DCACHE_CACHE_EN_BIT |
182	                  DCACHE_CACHE_ENTRY_THRESH |
183	                  DCACHE_STB_TIMEOUT_EN_BIT;
184	
185	  /* Enable store buffer timeout */
186	
187	  *dcache_stb = 1;
188	
189	  /* Wait for cache initialization to finish */
190	
191	  while ((*dcache_status & DCACHE_INIT_FINISH_BIT) == 0)
192	    {
193	      if (timeout-- == 0)
194	        {
195	          return false;
196	        }
197	    }
198	
199	  /* Clear bypass to enable caching */
200	
201	  *dcache_ctrl &= ~DCACHE_CACHE_BYPASS_BIT;
202	  return true;
203	}

92	      return 0;

23	/****************************************************************************
24	 * RV1126B HPMCU IRQ dispatch for NuttX
25	 *
26	 * This file implements the RISC-V interrupt dispatch logic for the
27	 * RV1126B HPMCU.  The SCR1 core uses the IPIC (CSR 0xbf0..0xbf7) for
28	 * interrupt prioritization and EOI/SOI handshaking, and the INTMUX
29	 * for external interrupt routing.
30	 *
31	 * Dispatch flow:
32	 *   1. Trap entry (rv1126b_head.S g_traps) saves context and calls
33	 *      riscv_dispatch_irq(mcause, regs).
34	 *   2. riscv_dispatch_irq() identifies the interrupt type and:
35	 *      - For timer interrupts (mcause=7): calls up_timer_int()
36	 *        and returns regs.
37	 *      - For external interrupts (mcause=11): scans INTMUX status
38	 *        registers to find the active IRQs, then dispatches each
39	 *        via riscv_doirq(irq, regs) (which handles context switch
40	 *        bookkeeping), wrapped by IPIC SOI/EOI.
41	 *   3. The returned regs pointer is used by the assembly trap exit
42	 *      to restore the (possibly switched) context.

113	 *
114	 * Description:
115	 *   Scan the INTMUX status registers to find the highest-priority
116	 *   active (pending and enabled) IRQ.
117	 *
118	 * Returned Value:
119	 *   IRQ number (0..255), or -1 if no active IRQ is found.
120	 *

122	
123	static int rv1126b_get_active_irq(void)
124	{
125	  int i;
126	  unsigned int status;
127	
128	  for (i = 0; i < INTMUX_NGROUPS; i++)
129	    {
130	      status = getreg32(RV1126B_INTMUX_BASE +
131	                         RV1126B_INTMUX_STATUS_OFFSET +
132	                         (i * RV1126B_INTMUX_GROUP_STRIDE));
133	      if (status != 0)
134	        {
135	          /* Find the lowest-numbered (highest priority) set bit */
136	
137	          int bit = __builtin_ctz(status);
138	          return i * INTMUX_IRQS_PER_GROUP + bit;
139	        }
140	    }
141	
142	  return -1;
143	}
