/****************************************************************************
 * Name: rv1126b_dcache_init
 *
 * Description:
 *   Initialize the HPMCU DCache:
 *   - Configure the uncache address region via GRF_SYS so that
 *     memory-mapped peripherals (0x20000..0x23000) bypass the cache.
 *   - Enable DCache with store buffer (stb_entry=7, timeout enabled).
 *   - Wait for cache initialization to complete.
 *   - Clear the cache bypass bit to enable caching.
 *
 *   Note: Do not access uninitialized global variables before this
 *   function completes, as BSS must already be zeroed.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

static bool rv1126b_dcache_init(void)
{
  volatile uint32_t *grf_cache_start =
    (volatile uint32_t *)GRF_HPMCU_CACHE_ADDR_START;
  volatile uint32_t *grf_cache_end =
    (volatile uint32_t *)GRF_HPMCU_CACHE_ADDR_END;
  volatile uint32_t *dcache_ctrl =
    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_CACHE_CTRL;
  volatile uint32_t *dcache_status =
    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_CACHE_STATUS;
  volatile uint32_t *dcache_stb =
    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_STB_TIMEOUT_CTRL;
  volatile uint32_t timeout = RV1126B_DIAG_POLL_TIMEOUT;

  /* Set the uncache region to cover peripheral address space */

  *grf_cache_start = 0x20000;
  *grf_cache_end   = 0x23000;

  /* Enable DCache: cache_en=1, stb_entry=7, stb_timeout_en=1 */

  *dcache_ctrl |= DCACHE_CACHE_EN_BIT |
                  DCACHE_CACHE_ENTRY_THRESH |
                  DCACHE_STB_TIMEOUT_EN_BIT;

  /* Enable store buffer timeout */

  *dcache_stb = 1;

  /* Wait for cache initialization to finish */

  while ((*dcache_status & DCACHE_INIT_FINISH_BIT) == 0)
    {
      if (timeout-- == 0)
        {
          return false;
        }
    }

  /* Clear bypass to enable caching */

  *dcache_ctrl &= ~DCACHE_CACHE_BYPASS_BIT;
  return true;
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Functions
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: rv1126b_start
 *
 * Description:
 *   C entry point called from rv1126b_head.S _start.
 *   Performs all hardware and OS initialization, then transfers control
 *   to the NuttX kernel.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

void rv1126b_start(void)
{
  /* Initialize early UART before BSS/data/cache setup. */

  rv1126b_lowsetup();

  /* 1. Initialize BSS section. */

  rv1126b_bss_init();

  /* 2. Initialize data section (copy from ROM/flash to RAM) */

  rv1126b_data_init();

  /* 3. Preserve the current DCache initialization policy. */

  if (!RV1126B_DIAG_SKIP_DCACHE)
    {
      (void)rv1126b_dcache_init();
    }

  /* 4. Configure clocks: GPLL 1188 MHz, HPMCU 396 MHz */

  rv1126b_clockconfig();

  /* 5. Board-level initialization */

  boardinitialize();

  /* 6. Start the NuttX kernel -- this call does not return */

  nx_start();

  for (; ; )
    {
    }
}

/****************************************************************************
 * RV1126B HPMCU IRQ dispatch for NuttX
 *
 * This file implements the RISC-V interrupt dispatch logic for the
 * RV1126B HPMCU.  The SCR1 core uses the IPIC (CSR 0xbf0..0xbf7) for
 * interrupt prioritization and EOI/SOI handshaking, and the INTMUX
 * for external interrupt routing.
 *
 * Dispatch flow:
 *   1. Trap entry (rv1126b_head.S g_traps) saves context and calls
 *      riscv_dispatch_irq(mcause, regs).
 *   2. riscv_dispatch_irq() identifies the interrupt type and:
 *      - For timer interrupts (mcause=7): calls up_timer_int()
 *        and returns regs.
 *      - For external interrupts (mcause=11): scans INTMUX status
 *        registers to find the active IRQs, then dispatches each
 *        via riscv_doirq(irq, regs) (which handles context switch
 *        bookkeeping), wrapped by IPIC SOI/EOI.
 *   3. The returned regs pointer is used by the assembly trap exit
 *      to restore the (possibly switched) context.
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Included Files
 ****************************************************************************/

#include <nuttx/config.h>
#include <nuttx/irq.h>
#include <nuttx/arch.h>

#include <stdint.h>

#include "riscv_internal.h"
#include "chip.h"

/****************************************************************************
 * Pre-processor Definitions
 ****************************************************************************/

/* INTMUX definitions from hardware/rv1126b_intmux.h */

#define INTMUX_NGROUPS          RV1126B_INTMUX_NGROUPS  /* 8 groups */
#define INTMUX_IRQS_PER_GROUP   32

/* RISC-V interrupt cause codes (from riscv_csr_encoding.h / chip.h) */

#define MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT   ((uintptr_t)1 << (sizeof(uintptr_t) * 8 - 1))
#define IRQ_M_TIMER            7
#define IRQ_M_EXT              11

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Function Prototypes
 ****************************************************************************/

void up_timer_int(void);

/****************************************************************************
 * Private Functions
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: rv1126b_ipic_soi
 *
 * Description:
 *   Write to IPIC SOI (Start of Interrupt) CSR to acknowledge the
 *   start of interrupt processing.  Any value can be written.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

static inline void rv1126b_ipic_soi(void)
{
  write_csr(0xbf5, 0);
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: rv1126b_ipic_eoi
 *
 * Description:
 *   Write to IPIC EOI (End of Interrupt) CSR to signal the end of
 *   interrupt processing.  Any value can be written.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

static inline void rv1126b_ipic_eoi(void)
{
  write_csr(0xbf4, 0);
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: rv1126b_get_active_irq
 *
 * Description:
 *   Scan the INTMUX status registers to find the highest-priority
 *   active (pending and enabled) IRQ.
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   IRQ number (0..255), or -1 if no active IRQ is found.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

static int rv1126b_get_active_irq(void)
{
  int i;
  unsigned int status;

  for (i = 0; i < INTMUX_NGROUPS; i++)
    {
      status = getreg32(RV1126B_INTMUX_BASE +
                         RV1126B_INTMUX_STATUS_OFFSET +
                         (i * RV1126B_INTMUX_GROUP_STRIDE));
      if (status != 0)
        {
          /* Find the lowest-numbered (highest priority) set bit */

          int bit = __builtin_ctz(status);
          return i * INTMUX_IRQS_PER_GROUP + bit;
        }
    }

  return -1;
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Functions
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: riscv_dispatch_irq
 *
 * Description:
 *   Dispatch an interrupt based on the mcause value.
 *
 *   This function is called from the NuttX RISC-V common interrupt
 *   handling path (riscv_doirq -> riscv_dispatch_irq) when the mcause
 *   indicates an interrupt (bit 31 set).
 *
 *   For the RV1126B HPMCU:
 *     - mcause == 7  (IRQ_M_TIMER): machine timer interrupt
 *     - mcause == 11 (IRQ_M_EXT):   machine external interrupt
 *       (routed through INTMUX)
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   mcause - The value of the mcause CSR
 *   regs   - Pointer to the saved register context
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   Pointer to the (possibly new) register context after dispatch.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

void *riscv_dispatch_irq(uintptr_t mcause, uintreg_t *regs)
{
  uintptr_t cause;

  if ((mcause & MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT) == 0)
    {
      /* Synchronous exceptions must go through riscv_doirq() so NuttX can
       * advance mepc for ecall and handle context switching properly.
       */

      regs = riscv_doirq((int)mcause, regs);
      return regs;
    }

  /* Interrupt: strip the interrupt bit to get the cause code */

  cause = mcause & ~MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT;

  if (cause == IRQ_M_TIMER)
    {
      /* Machine timer interrupt -- call the NuttX timer handler */

      up_timer_int();
    }
  else if (cause == IRQ_M_EXT)
    {
      /* Machine external interrupt -- scan INTMUX for active IRQs */

      int irq;

      /* Signal IPIC Start of Interrupt */

      rv1126b_ipic_soi();

      /* Scan for active IRQs -- handle all pending IRQs in this group */

      while ((irq = rv1126b_get_active_irq()) >= 0)
        {
          /* Dispatch through the NuttX IRQ dispatch table.
           * riscv_doirq() handles context switch bookkeeping and
           * returns the (possibly updated) regs pointer.
           */

          regs = riscv_doirq(irq, regs);
        }

      /* Signal IPIC End of Interrupt */

      rv1126b_ipic_eoi();
    }
  else
    {
      /* Unexpected interrupt cause -- spin */

      for (; ; );
    }

  return regs;
}

46	/* GPLL (General PLL) registers at TOPCRU
47	 *
48	 * SDK-confirmed layout (rv1126b.h TOPCRU_REG):
49	 *   AUPLL_CON[5] at offset 0x0000 (5 registers, 20 bytes)
50	 *   GPLL_CON[5]  at offset 0x0020
51	 *
52	 * GPLL_CON0: PLL divisor, multiplier, and lock status
53	 *   Bit 31: LOCK (read-only, 1 = PLL is locked)
54	 *
55	 * PLL output = (24 MHz / refdiv) * fbdiv / postdiv1 / postdiv2
56	 * For 1188 MHz: refdiv=1, fbdiv=99, postdiv1=2, postdiv2=1
57	 *   (24/1) * 99 / 2 = 1188 MHz
58	 */
59	
60	#define GPLL_CON0_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x0020)  /* GPLL_CON[0] */
61	#define GPLL_CON1_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x0024)  /* GPLL_CON[1] */
62	#define GPLL_CON2_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x0028)  /* GPLL_CON[2] */
63	#define GPLL_CON3_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x002c)  /* GPLL_CON[3] */
64	#define GPLL_CON4_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x0030)  /* GPLL_CON[4] */

66	/* HPMCU clock source selection
67	 * CLK_HPMCU is a gated clock from aclk_bus_root (no mux/divider).
68	 * SDK-verified: SCR1_CORE_FREQUECY = 396 MHz (GPLL 1188 MHz / 3).
69	 * The divider is configured by A-core/bootrom; HPMCU does not need
70	 * to write to CORECRU CLKSEL_CON00 (those bits belong to A53 core).
71	 */

83	/****************************************************************************
84	 * Name: rv1126b_wait_pll_lock
85	 *
86	 * Description:
87	 *   Wait for the PLL to achieve lock by polling the lock bit.
88	 *
89	 * Returned Value:
90	 *   true if PLL locked within the timeout, false otherwise.
91	 *
92	 ****************************************************************************/
93	
94	static bool rv1126b_wait_pll_lock(uint32_t pll_lock_addr)
95	{
96	  volatile uint32_t timeout = 1000000;
97	
98	  while (timeout > 0)
99	    {
100	      if (getreg32(pll_lock_addr) & GPLL_LOCK_MASK)
101	        {

/* PLL configuration registers */

#define TOPCRU_BASE           RV1126B_TOPCRU_BASE

/* GPLL (General PLL) registers at TOPCRU
 *
 * SDK-confirmed layout (rv1126b.h TOPCRU_REG):
 *   AUPLL_CON[5] at offset 0x0000 (5 registers, 20 bytes)
 *   GPLL_CON[5]  at offset 0x0020
 *
 * GPLL_CON0: PLL divisor, multiplier, and lock status
 *   Bit 31: LOCK (read-only, 1 = PLL is locked)
 *
 * PLL output = (24 MHz / refdiv) * fbdiv / postdiv1 / postdiv2
 * For 1188 MHz: refdiv=1, fbdiv=99, postdiv1=2, postdiv2=1
 *   (24/1) * 99 / 2 = 1188 MHz
 */

#define GPLL_CON0_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x0020)  /* GPLL_CON[0] */
#define GPLL_CON1_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x0024)  /* GPLL_CON[1] */
#define GPLL_CON2_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x0028)  /* GPLL_CON[2] */
#define GPLL_CON3_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x002c)  /* GPLL_CON[3] */
#define GPLL_CON4_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x0030)  /* GPLL_CON[4] */

/* HPMCU clock source selection
 * CLK_HPMCU is a gated clock from aclk_bus_root (no mux/divider).
 * SDK-verified: SCR1_CORE_FREQUECY = 396 MHz (GPLL 1188 MHz / 3).
 * The divider is configured by A-core/bootrom; HPMCU does not need
 * to write to CORECRU CLKSEL_CON00 (those bits belong to A53 core).
 */

/* SDK-verified: GPLL lock status is at GPLL_CON[2] bit 10 (TOPCRU + 0x28) */

#define GPLL_LOCK_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x0028)
#define GPLL_LOCK_SHIFT       10
#define GPLL_LOCK_MASK        (1 << GPLL_LOCK_SHIFT)

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: rv1126b_wait_pll_lock
 *
 * Description:
 *   Wait for the PLL to achieve lock by polling the lock bit.
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   true if PLL locked within the timeout, false otherwise.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

static bool rv1126b_wait_pll_lock(uint32_t pll_lock_addr)
{
  volatile uint32_t timeout = 1000000;

  while (timeout > 0)
    {
      if (getreg32(pll_lock_addr) & GPLL_LOCK_MASK)
        {
          return true;  /* PLL locked */
        }

      timeout--;
    }

  return false;  /* Timeout -- PLL did not lock */
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: rv1126b_ensure_gpll_locked
 *
 * Description:
 *   Verify that GPLL is already locked at 1188 MHz.  In an AMP
 *   environment the Linux A-core (or bootrom) will have configured
 *   GPLL before the HPMCU starts.  We do NOT reconfigure GPLL here
 *   to avoid interfering with other cores that depend on it.
 *
 *   If GPLL is not locked, let the caller return without changing clocks.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

static bool rv1126b_ensure_gpll_locked(void)
{
  if (!rv1126b_wait_pll_lock(GPLL_LOCK_ADDR))
    {
      return false;
    }

  return true;
}

 *
 *   On the RV1126B, CLK_HPMCU is a gated clock sourced from aclk_bus_root
 *   (confirmed by the Linux CRU driver: GATE(CLK_HPMCU, "clk_hpmcu",
 *   "aclk_bus_root", ...)).  The clock source selection and divider are
 *   configured by the A-core Linux or bootrom before the HPMCU starts.
 *
 *   SDK-verified: SCR1_CORE_FREQUECY = 396 MHz, GPLL = 1188 MHz.
 *   The ratio 1188/3 = 396 MHz matches, but we do NOT write to
 *   CORECRU CLKSEL_CON00 because bits [5:0] are allocated to the A53
 *   core clock (CLK_CORE_PVTPLL_SRC_SEL, CLK_CORE_SRC_SEL) per the
 *   SDK header rv1126b.h, not to the HPMCU.
 *

static void rv1126b_set_hpmcu_clock(void)
{
  /* HPMCU clock is pre-configured by A-core/bootrom.
   * No register writes needed -- aclk_bus_root is already set.
   * If in the future this needs explicit configuration, the correct
   * register and bit fields must be determined from the TRM.
   */
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: rv1126b_clockconfig
 *
 * Description:
 *   Configure the system clocks for the RV1126B HPMCU.
 *
 *   This function is called from rv1126b_start() very early in the boot
 *   sequence.  In an AMP environment, GPLL is already configured by the
 *   Linux A-core or bootrom.  This function:
 *     1. Verifies GPLL is locked at 1188 MHz (does NOT reconfigure it)
 *     2. Sets HPMCU core clock to 396 MHz (GPLL / 3)
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

void rv1126b_clockconfig(void)
{
  /* Step 1: Verify GPLL is locked (already configured by A-core/bootrom).
   * Do NOT reconfigure GPLL to avoid disrupting Linux on the A-core.
   * If GPLL is not locked, leave clocks unchanged.
   */

  if (!rv1126b_ensure_gpll_locked())
    {
      return;
    }

  /* Step 2: HPMCU clock is pre-configured to 396 MHz (GPLL / 3) by
   * the A-core or bootrom.  CLK_HPMCU is a gate from aclk_bus_root;
   * no explicit divider configuration is needed or safe here.
   */

  rv1126b_set_hpmcu_clock();
}

bool __atomic_compare_exchange_4(volatile void *ptr, void *expected,
                                 uint32_t desired, bool weak,
                                 int success_memorder, int failure_memorder)
{
  uint32_t *ep = (uint32_t *)expected;
  volatile uint32_t *pp = (volatile uint32_t *)ptr;
  uint32_t old = *ep;

  if (*pp == old)
    {
      *pp = desired;
      return true;
    }

  *ep = *pp;
  return false;
}

uint32_t __atomic_fetch_add_4(volatile void *ptr, uint32_t val,
                              int memorder)
{
  volatile uint32_t *pp = (volatile uint32_t *)ptr;
  uint32_t old = *pp;
  *pp = old + val;
  return old;
}

uint32_t __atomic_fetch_sub_4(volatile void *ptr, uint32_t val,
                              int memorder)
{
  volatile uint32_t *pp = (volatile uint32_t *)ptr;
  uint32_t old = *pp;
  *pp = old - val;
  return old;
}

uint32_t __atomic_fetch_or_4(volatile void *ptr, uint32_t val,
                             int memorder)
{
  volatile uint32_t *pp = (volatile uint32_t *)ptr;
  uint32_t old = *pp;
  *pp = old | val;
  return old;
}

uint32_t __atomic_fetch_and_4(volatile void *ptr, uint32_t val,
                              int memorder)
{
  volatile uint32_t *pp = (volatile uint32_t *)ptr;
  uint32_t old = *pp;
  *pp = old & val;
  return old;
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Included Files
 ****************************************************************************/

#include <nuttx/config.h>

#include <stdint.h>

#include <nuttx/arch.h>
#include <nuttx/clock.h>
#include <nuttx/timers/arch_timer.h>

#include "riscv_internal.h"
#include "hardware/rv1126b_timer.h"
#include "chip.h"

/****************************************************************************
 * Pre-processor Definitions
 ****************************************************************************/

/* MTIME register access macros */

#define CTIMER_MTIME_CTRL   (RV1126B_CTIMER_BASE + RV1126B_CTIMER_MTIME_CTRL)
#define CTIMER_MTIME_DIV    (RV1126B_CTIMER_BASE + RV1126B_CTIMER_MTIME_DIV)
#define CTIMER_MTIME        (RV1126B_CTIMER_BASE + RV1126B_CTIMER_MTIME)
#define CTIMER_MTIMEH       (RV1126B_CTIMER_BASE + RV1126B_CTIMER_MTIMEH)
#define CTIMER_MTIMECMP     (RV1126B_CTIMER_BASE + RV1126B_CTIMER_MTIMECMP)
#define CTIMER_MTIMECMPH    (RV1126B_CTIMER_BASE + RV1126B_CTIMER_MTIMECMPH)

/* Timer configuration:
 * HPMCU frequency = 396 MHz
 * Divider = 1000
 * Effective timer clock = 396 MHz / 1000 = 396 kHz
 * For 100 Hz tick: 396000 / 100 = 3960 counts per tick
 */

#define RV1126B_MTIME_DIV_VALUE   1000
#define RV1126B_MTIME_TICK_VALUE  (RV1126B_MTIME_FREQ / RV1126B_MTIME_DIV_VALUE / 100)

/****************************************************************************
 * Private Data
 ****************************************************************************/

static uint64_t g_mtimecmp_step = RV1126B_MTIME_TICK_VALUE;

/****************************************************************************
 * Private Functions
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: rv1126b_timer_stop
 *
 * Description:
 *   Stop the MTIME timer by clearing the enable bit.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

static void rv1126b_timer_stop(void)
{
  uint32_t regval;

  regval = getreg32(CTIMER_MTIME_CTRL);
  regval &= ~RV1126B_MTIME_CTRL_EN;
  putreg32(regval, CTIMER_MTIME_CTRL);
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: rv1126b_timer_start
 *
 * Description:
 *   Start the MTIME timer by setting the enable bit.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

static void rv1126b_timer_start(void)
{
  uint32_t regval;

  regval = getreg32(CTIMER_MTIME_CTRL);
  regval |= RV1126B_MTIME_CTRL_EN;
  putreg32(regval, CTIMER_MTIME_CTRL);
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Functions
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: up_timer_initialize
 *
 * Description:
 *   Configure the MTIME timer to generate periodic system tick interrupts
 *   at 100 Hz (CONFIG_USEC_PER_TICK = 10000 usec).
 *
 *   This function is called during early OS initialization before the
 *   scheduler is started.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

void up_timer_initialize(void)
{
  /* Stop the timer first */

  rv1126b_timer_stop();

  /* Reset MTIME counter to 0 */

  putreg32(0, CTIMER_MTIME);
  putreg32(0, CTIMER_MTIMEH);

  /* Reset MTIMECMP to 0 */

  putreg32(0, CTIMER_MTIMECMP);
  putreg32(0, CTIMER_MTIMECMPH);

  /* Set the divider to divide the core clock by 1000 */

  putreg32(RV1126B_MTIME_DIV_VALUE, CTIMER_MTIME_DIV);

  /* Set MTIMECMP to the first tick value */

  putreg32(RV1126B_MTIME_TICK_VALUE, CTIMER_MTIMECMP);
  putreg32(0, CTIMER_MTIMECMPH);

  /* Enable the MIP_MTIP bit in the mie CSR to allow timer interrupts */

  set_csr(mie, MIP_MTIP);

  /* Start the timer */

  rv1126b_timer_start();
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: up_timer_int
 *
 * Description:
 *   Advance the MTIMECMP register by one tick period.  This is called
 *   from the timer interrupt handler to acknowledge the interrupt and
 *   schedule the next tick.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

void up_timer_int(void)
{
  uint64_t mtime;
  uint64_t mtimecmp;

  /* Temporarily disable timer interrupt to avoid race condition */

  clear_csr(mie, MIP_MTIP);

  /* Read current mtime and advance compare from it (not from old mtimecmp) */

  mtime = (uint64_t)getreg32(CTIMER_MTIMEH) << 32;
  mtime |= getreg32(CTIMER_MTIME);
  mtimecmp = mtime + g_mtimecmp_step;

  /* Write new MTIMECMP value */

  putreg32((uint32_t)(mtimecmp & 0xffffffff), CTIMER_MTIMECMP);
  putreg32((uint32_t)(mtimecmp >> 32), CTIMER_MTIMECMPH);

  /* Process the OS tick */

  nxsched_process_timer();

  /* Re-enable timer interrupt */

  set_csr(mie, MIP_MTIP);
}

 * NuttX - RV1126B BSP Configuration
 *
 * Console UART selection, clock rate, and baud rate definitions shared
 * between the early lowputc driver and the full serial driver.
 *
 * This BSP uses a custom rv1126b_serial.c driver rather than the generic
 * 16550 driver, so CONFIG_16550_UART is NOT required.
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifndef __BOARD_CHIP_RV1126B_CONFIG_H
#define __BOARD_CHIP_RV1126B_CONFIG_H

/****************************************************************************
 * Pre-processor Definitions
 ****************************************************************************/

/* UART configuration
 *
 * This BSP uses a custom rv1126b_serial.c driver rather than the generic
 * 16550 driver.  The console is selected via CONFIG_RV1126B_UART5_CONSOLE
 * defined in the chip Kconfig.
 */

#if defined(CONFIG_RV1126B_UART5_CONSOLE)
#  define HAVE_UART           1
#  define HAVE_SERIAL_CONSOLE 1
#  define CONSOLE_UART        5
#  define CONSOLE_BASE        RV1126B_UART5_BASE
#else
#  define HAVE_UART           0
#  define HAVE_SERIAL_CONSOLE 0
#endif

/* GPIO configuration */

#if defined(CONFIG_DEV_GPIO)
#  define HAVE_GPIO           1
#else
#  define HAVE_GPIO           0
#endif

/* Timer configuration */

#define HAVE_TIMER            1
#define TIMER_FREQUENCY       396000000  /* 396 MHz timer input clock */

/* UART5 source clock rate (24 MHz oscillator, SDK-verified) */

#define CONSOLE_CLK_RATE      24000000

/* Console baud rate and divisor latch value.
 * SDK default for all UARTs on this SoC is 1500000 baud.
 */

#define CONSOLE_BAUD_RATE     1500000

#define CONSOLE_DIVISOR       (CONSOLE_CLK_RATE / 16 / CONSOLE_BAUD_RATE)

#endif /* __BOARD_CHIP_RV1126B_CONFIG_H */

40	/****************************************************************************
41	 * RISC-V CSR Helper Macros
42	 *
43	 * These are needed for inline CSR access in C code (set_csr, clear_csr,
44	 * read_csr, write_csr).  They follow the same pattern as the SDK
45	 * riscv_csr_encoding.h.
46	 ****************************************************************************/
47	
48	#ifndef __ASSEMBLY__
49	
50	#ifdef __GNUC__
51	
52	#define read_csr(reg) \
53	  ({ unsigned long __tmp; \
54	     asm volatile ("csrr %0, " #reg : "=r"(__tmp)); \
55	     __tmp; })
56	
57	#define write_csr(reg, val) \
58	  ({ asm volatile ("csrw " #reg ", %0" :: "rK"(val)); })
59	
60	#define set_csr(reg, bit) \
61	  ({ unsigned long __tmp; \
62	     asm volatile ("csrrs %0, " #reg ", %1" : "=r"(__tmp) : "rK"(bit)); \
63	     __tmp; })
64	
65	#define clear_csr(reg, bit) \
66	  ({ unsigned long __tmp; \
67	     asm volatile ("csrrc %0, " #reg ", %1" : "=r"(__tmp) : "rK"(bit)); \
68	     __tmp; })
69	
70	#endif /* __GNUC__ */

/****************************************************************************

 ****************************************************************************/

/* Hardware register definitions */

#include "hardware/rv1126b_intmux.h"

#include "hardware/rv1126b_uart.h"
#include "hardware/rv1126b_cru.h"

/****************************************************************************
 * RISC-V CSR Helper Macros
 *
 * These are needed for inline CSR access in C code (set_csr, clear_csr,
 * read_csr, write_csr).  They follow the same pattern as the SDK
 * riscv_csr_encoding.h.
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifndef __ASSEMBLY__

#ifdef __GNUC__

#define read_csr(reg) \
  ({ unsigned long __tmp; \
     asm volatile ("csrr %0, " #reg : "=r"(__tmp)); \
     __tmp; })

#define write_csr(reg, val) \
  ({ asm volatile ("csrw " #reg ", %0" :: "rK"(val)); })

#define set_csr(reg, bit) \
  ({ unsigned long __tmp; \
     asm volatile ("csrrs %0, " #reg ", %1" : "=r"(__tmp) : "rK"(bit)); \
     __tmp; })

#define clear_csr(reg, bit) \
  ({ unsigned long __tmp; \
     asm volatile ("csrrc %0, " #reg ", %1" : "=r"(__tmp) : "rK"(bit)); \
     __tmp; })

#endif /* __GNUC__ */

/****************************************************************************
 * MSTATUS and MIP bit definitions
 *
 * These supplement the CSR macros for interrupt control.
 ****************************************************************************/

#define MSTATUS_MIE     0x00000008
#define MIP_MEIP        0x00000800  /* Machine external interrupt pending */
#define MIP_MTIP        0x00000080  /* Machine timer interrupt pending */
#define MIP_MSIP        0x00000008  /* Machine software interrupt pending */

/****************************************************************************
 * RISC-V Interrupt Cause Codes
 ****************************************************************************/

#define IRQ_M_SOFT      3
#define IRQ_M_TIMER     7
#define IRQ_M_EXT       11

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Function Prototypes
 ****************************************************************************/

void rv1126b_start(void);
void rv1126b_lowsetup(void);   /* Early UART5 init from rv1126b_lowputc.c */
void rv1126b_clockconfig(void); /* Clock config from rv1126b_clockconfig.c */

#endif /* !__ASSEMBLY__ */

83	/* IRQ Stack Frame Format
84	 *
85	 * This stack frame is created on each interrupt.  These registers are stored
86	 * in the TCB to many context switches.
87	 *
88	 * The following represent all of the "static" registers r8-r15.  These
89	 * are registers that whose value must be retained across function calls.
90	 * These registers must be saved bothby interrupt handling context switch
91	 * switch logic and also by user-initiated context switches.
92	 *
93	 * Registers are saved in the order consistent with pushmho <r8-r15>,
94	 * that is with r15 pushed first and r8 push last.  Since the z16f has
95	 * a "push-down" stack, the registers will be "in order" in memory.
96	 */
97	
98	#define REG_R8              ( 0) /* 32-bits: R8 */
99	#define REG_R9              ( 2) /* 32-bits: R9 */
100	#define REG_R10             ( 4) /* 32-bits: R10 */
101	#define REG_R11             ( 6) /* 32-bits: R11 */
102	#define REG_R12             ( 8) /* 32-bits: R12 */
103	#define REG_R13             (10) /* 32-bits: R13 */
104	
105	/* The frame pointer and the SP at the point of task resumption must
106	 * always be saved.
107	 */
108	
109	#define REG_R14             (12) /* 32-bits: R14 = fp */
110	#define REG_FP              REG_R14
111	#define REG_R15             (14) /* 32-bits: R15 = sp */
112	#define REG_SP              REG_R15
113	
114	/* The following represent all of the "volatile" registers r0-r7.  These
115	 * are registers that whose value need not be retained across function
116	 * calls.  These registers must be saved by interrupt handling context
117	 * switch logic but not by user-initiated context switches.
118	 *
119	 * Registers are saved in the order consistent with pushmlo <r0-r7>,
120	 * that is with r7 pushed first and r0 push last.  Since the z16f has
121	 * a "push-down" stack, the registers will be "in order" in memory.
122	 */

124	#define REG_R0              (16) /* 32-bits: R0 */
125	#define REG_R1              (18) /* 32-bits: R1 */
126	#define REG_R2              (20) /* 32-bits: R2 */
127	#define REG_R3              (22) /* 32-bits: R3 */
128	#define REG_R4              (24) /* 32-bits: R4 */
129	#define REG_R5              (26) /* 32-bits: R5 */
130	#define REG_R6              (28) /* 32-bits: R6 */

		AT32F437-MINI board based on the Artery AT32F437VMT7 MCU.

config ARCH_BOARD_CUSTOM
	bool "Custom development board"
	---help---
		Select this option if there is no directory for the board under boards/.

		Don't see the board you want?  You must first select the exact MCU part
		number, then the boards supporting that part will be available for selection.

endchoice

if ARCH_BOARD_CUSTOM
menu "Custom Board Configuration"

config ARCH_BOARD_CUSTOM_NAME
	string "Custom board name"
	default ""
	---help---
		This is a name for the board.  It is not used except to return the
		information via the NSH uname command.

config ARCH_BOARD_CUSTOM_DIR
	string "Custom board directory"
	default ""
	---help---
		If the custom board configuration is selected, then it is necessary
		to also tell the build system where it can find the board directory
		for the custom board.

		In this case, the board directory is assumed to lie outside the
		NuttX directory.  The provided path must then be a full, absolute
		path to some location outside of the NuttX source tree (like
		"~/projects/myboard").

config ARCH_BOARD_CUSTOM_DIR_RELPATH
	bool "Relative custom board directory"
	default y
	---help---
		Specifies that the board directory is relative to the NuttX directory.

config BOARD_CUSTOM_LEDS
	bool "Custom board LEDs"
	default n
	select ARCH_HAVE_LEDS

config BOARD_CUSTOM_BUTTONS
	bool "Custom board buttons"
	default n
	select ARCH_HAVE_BUTTONS
	select ARCH_BUTTONS

config BOARD_CUSTOM_IRQBUTTONS
	bool "Custom Board IRQ buttons"
	default n
	depends on BOARD_CUSTOM_BUTTONS
	select ARCH_HAVE_IRQBUTTONS
	select ARCH_IRQBUTTONS

config BOARD_CUSTOM_INTERRUPT
	bool "Custom board PHY interrupts"
	default n
	depends on NETDEVICES
	select ARCH_PHY_INTERRUPT

endmenu # Custom Board Configuration
endif #ARCH_BOARD_CUSTOM

  nuttx_create_symlink(${NUTTX_CHIP_ABS_DIR}
                       ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/arch/${CONFIG_ARCH}/src/chip)
endif()

# Unsupport custom board/chips yet, workaround

if(NOT EXISTS ${NUTTX_APPS_BINDIR}/platform/board/Kconfig)
  file(MAKE_DIRECTORY ${NUTTX_APPS_BINDIR}/platform/board)
  file(TOUCH ${NUTTX_APPS_BINDIR}/platform/board/Kconfig)
endif()

if(NOT EXISTS ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/.config OR NOT "${NUTTX_DEFCONFIG}" STREQUAL
                                             "${NUTTX_DEFCONFIG_SAVED}")

  message(STATUS "Initializing NuttX")
  configure_file(${NUTTX_DEFCONFIG} defconfig COPYONLY)
  configure_file(${NUTTX_DEFCONFIG} .config.compressed COPYONLY)

  set(ENV{KCONFIG_CONFIG} ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/.config.compressed)

  # Do olddefconfig step to expand the abbreviated defconfig into normal config
  nuttx_olddefconfig()

  file(RENAME ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/.config.compressed
       ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/.config)
  set(ENV{KCONFIG_CONFIG} ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/.config)

  # store original expanded .config
  configure_file(${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/.config ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/.config.orig
                 COPYONLY)

  # We define host
  nuttx_sethost()

  set(NUTTX_DEFCONFIG_SAVED
      ${NUTTX_DEFCONFIG}
      CACHE INTERNAL "Saved defconfig path" FORCE)

  # Print configuration choices
  message(STATUS "  CMake:  ${CMAKE_VERSION}")
  if(CMAKE_GENERATOR MATCHES "Ninja")

      OUTPUT_VARIABLE ninja_version
      OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE)

endif()

23	/****************************************************************************
24	 * RV1126B HPMCU (RISC-V SCR1) startup assembly for NuttX
25	 *
26	 * Provides:
27	 *   - __start: primary entry point
28	 *   - g_traps: trap vector for interrupts and exceptions
29	 *
30	 * Based on the Rockchip RV1126B SDK CMSIS startup template and
31	 * NuttX RISC-V conventions.
32	 *
33	 * Register layout must match nuttx/arch/risc-v/include/irq.h
34	 * (RV32, no CLIC, no shadow stack):
35	 *
36	 *   Slot  0        (offset   0) : REG_EPC     -- mepc
37	 *   Slot  1        (offset   4) : REG_X1      -- x1 (ra)
38	 *   Slot  2        (offset   8) : REG_X2      -- x2 (sp)
39	 *   ...
40	 *   Slot 31        (offset 124) : REG_X31     -- x31 (t6)
41	 *   Slot 32        (offset 128) : REG_INT_CTX -- mstatus
42	 *   Total: XCPTCONTEXT_REGS = 33, XCPTCONTEXT_SIZE = 132
43	 ****************************************************************************/
44	
45	#include <nuttx/config.h>
46	
47	/* Register save/restore width for RV32 */
48	
49	#define REGBYTES    4
50	#define RV32_REGBYTES   REGBYTES
51	
52	/* NuttX RISC-V trap frame layout (no CLIC, no shadow stack).
53	 * These MUST match nuttx/arch/risc-v/include/irq.h.
54	 * Include <arch/irq.h> instead of redefining when the build tree
55	 * supports it; local defines kept for build-tree independence.
56	 */
57	
58	#define REG_EPC_NDX         0
59	#define REG_X1_NDX          1
60	#define REG_X2_NDX          2
61	#define REG_INT_CTX_NDX    32
62	#define XCPTCONTEXT_REGS    33
63	#define XCPTCONTEXT_SIZE    (XCPTCONTEXT_REGS * REGBYTES)
64

/****************************************************************************
 * RV1126B HPMCU (RISC-V SCR1) startup assembly for NuttX
 *
 * Provides:
 *   - __start: primary entry point
 *   - g_traps: trap vector for interrupts and exceptions
 *
 * Based on the Rockchip RV1126B SDK CMSIS startup template and
 * NuttX RISC-V conventions.
 *
 * Register layout must match nuttx/arch/risc-v/include/irq.h
 * (RV32, no CLIC, no shadow stack):
 *
 *   Slot  0        (offset   0) : REG_EPC     -- mepc
 *   Slot  1        (offset   4) : REG_X1      -- x1 (ra)
 *   Slot  2        (offset   8) : REG_X2      -- x2 (sp)
 *   ...
 *   Slot 31        (offset 124) : REG_X31     -- x31 (t6)
 *   Slot 32        (offset 128) : REG_INT_CTX -- mstatus
 *   Total: XCPTCONTEXT_REGS = 33, XCPTCONTEXT_SIZE = 132
 ****************************************************************************/

#include <nuttx/config.h>

/* Register save/restore width for RV32 */

#define REGBYTES    4
#define RV32_REGBYTES   REGBYTES

/* NuttX RISC-V trap frame layout (no CLIC, no shadow stack).
 * These MUST match nuttx/arch/risc-v/include/irq.h.
 * Include <arch/irq.h> instead of redefining when the build tree
 * supports it; local defines kept for build-tree independence.
 */

#define REG_X1_NDX          1
#define REG_X2_NDX          2
#define REG_INT_CTX_NDX    32
#define XCPTCONTEXT_REGS    33
#define XCPTCONTEXT_SIZE    (XCPTCONTEXT_REGS * REGBYTES)

#define REG_EPC         (REGBYTES * REG_EPC_NDX)
#define REG_X1          (REGBYTES * REG_X1_NDX)
#define REG_X2          (REGBYTES * REG_X2_NDX)
#define REG_INT_CTX     (REGBYTES * REG_INT_CTX_NDX)

/* MSTATUS bits */

#define MSTATUS_MIE     0x00000008

/****************************************************************************

 ****************************************************************************/

    .section .text.start, "ax"
    .align  6
    .global __start
    .type   __start, %function

__start:

     * Convention: _gp = .sdata + 0x800

    .option pop

     * _ebss is the end of BSS; IDLETHREAD_STACKSIZE is configured by NuttX.

    la      sp, _ebss

    li      t0, MSTATUS_MIE

    la      t0, g_traps
    csrw    mtvec, t0

    call    rv1126b_start

/****************************************************************************

#include <nuttx/arch.h>
#include <nuttx/irq.h>

#include "riscv_mtimer.h"

/****************************************************************************
 * Private Types
 ****************************************************************************/

/* This structure provides the private representation of the "lower-half"
 * driver state structure.  This structure must be cast-compatible with the
 * oneshot_lowerhalf_s structure.
 */

struct riscv_mtimer_lowerhalf_s
{
  struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s lower;
  uintreg_t                  mtime;
  uintreg_t                  mtimecmp;
};

/****************************************************************************
 * Private Function Prototypes
 ****************************************************************************/

static clkcnt_t riscv_mtime_max_delay(struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower);
static clkcnt_t riscv_mtime_current(struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower);
static void riscv_mtime_start_absolute(struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower,
                                       clkcnt_t expected);
static void riscv_mtime_start(struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower,
                              clkcnt_t delta);
static void riscv_mtime_cancel(struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower);

/****************************************************************************
 * Private Data
 ****************************************************************************/

static const struct oneshot_operations_s g_riscv_mtimer_ops =
{
  .current        = riscv_mtime_current,
  .start          = riscv_mtime_start,
  .start_absolute = riscv_mtime_start_absolute,
  .cancel         = riscv_mtime_cancel,
  .max_delay      = riscv_mtime_max_delay
};

static struct riscv_mtimer_lowerhalf_s g_riscv_mtime_lowerhalf =
{
  .lower.ops = &g_riscv_mtimer_ops
};

/****************************************************************************
 * Private Functions
 ****************************************************************************/

static uint64_t riscv_mtimer_get_mtime(struct riscv_mtimer_lowerhalf_s *priv)
{
  return riscv_mtimer_get(priv->mtime);
}

static void riscv_mtimer_set_mtimecmp(struct riscv_mtimer_lowerhalf_s *priv,
                                      uint64_t value)
{
  riscv_mtimer_set(priv->mtime, priv->mtimecmp, value);
}

static clkcnt_t riscv_mtime_max_delay(struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower)
{
  return UINT64_MAX;
}

static clkcnt_t riscv_mtime_current(struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower)
{
  struct riscv_mtimer_lowerhalf_s *priv = &g_riscv_mtime_lowerhalf;
  return riscv_mtimer_get_mtime(priv);
}

static void riscv_mtime_start_absolute(struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower,
                                       clkcnt_t expected)
{
  struct riscv_mtimer_lowerhalf_s *priv = &g_riscv_mtime_lowerhalf;

  riscv_mtimer_set_mtimecmp(priv, expected);
}

static void riscv_mtime_start(struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower,
                              clkcnt_t delta)
{
  struct riscv_mtimer_lowerhalf_s *priv = &g_riscv_mtime_lowerhalf;
  irqstate_t flags = up_irq_save();
  uint64_t   curr  = riscv_mtimer_get_mtime(priv);

  riscv_mtimer_set_mtimecmp(priv, curr + delta);

  up_irq_restore(flags);
}

static void riscv_mtime_cancel(struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower)
{
  struct riscv_mtimer_lowerhalf_s *priv = &g_riscv_mtime_lowerhalf;
  riscv_mtimer_set_mtimecmp(priv, UINT64_MAX);
}

static int riscv_mtimer_interrupt(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
{
  struct riscv_mtimer_lowerhalf_s *priv = &g_riscv_mtime_lowerhalf;

  riscv_mtimer_set_mtimecmp(priv, UINT64_MAX);
  oneshot_process_callback(&priv->lower);

  return 0;
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Functions
 ****************************************************************************/

struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *
riscv_mtimer_initialize(uintreg_t mtime, uintreg_t mtimecmp,
                        int irq, uint64_t freq)
{
  struct riscv_mtimer_lowerhalf_s *priv = &g_riscv_mtime_lowerhalf;

  priv->mtime    = mtime;
  priv->mtimecmp = mtimecmp;

  oneshot_count_init(&priv->lower, freq);

  riscv_mtimer_set_mtimecmp(priv, UINT64_MAX);
  irq_attach(irq, riscv_mtimer_interrupt, priv);
  up_enable_irq(irq);

  return &priv->lower;
}

23	/****************************************************************************
24	 * RV1126B HPMCU IRQ dispatch for NuttX
25	 *
26	 * This file implements the RISC-V interrupt dispatch logic for the
27	 * RV1126B HPMCU.  The SCR1 core uses the IPIC (CSR 0xbf0..0xbf7) for
28	 * interrupt prioritization and EOI/SOI handshaking, and the INTMUX
29	 * for external interrupt routing.
30	 *
31	 * Dispatch flow:
32	 *   1. Trap entry (rv1126b_head.S g_traps) saves context and calls
33	 *      riscv_dispatch_irq(mcause, regs).
34	 *   2. riscv_dispatch_irq() identifies the interrupt type and:
35	 *      - For timer interrupts (mcause=7): calls up_timer_int()
36	 *        and returns regs.
37	 *      - For external interrupts (mcause=11): scans INTMUX status
38	 *        registers to find the active IRQs, then dispatches each
39	 *        via riscv_doirq(irq, regs) (which handles context switch
40	 *        bookkeeping), wrapped by IPIC SOI/EOI.
41	 *   3. The returned regs pointer is used by the assembly trap exit
42	 *      to restore the (possibly switched) context.
43	 ****************************************************************************/

111	/****************************************************************************
112	 * Name: rv1126b_get_active_irq
113	 *
114	 * Description:
115	 *   Scan the INTMUX status registers to find the highest-priority
116	 *   active (pending and enabled) IRQ.
117	 *
118	 * Returned Value:
119	 *   IRQ number (0..255), or -1 if no active IRQ is found.
120	 *
121	 ****************************************************************************/
122	
123	static int rv1126b_get_active_irq(void)
124	{
125	  int i;
126	  unsigned int status;
127	
128	  for (i = 0; i < INTMUX_NGROUPS; i++)
129	    {
130	      status = getreg32(RV1126B_INTMUX_BASE +
131	                         RV1126B_INTMUX_STATUS_OFFSET +
132	                         (i * RV1126B_INTMUX_GROUP_STRIDE));
133	      if (status != 0)
134	        {
135	          /* Find the lowest-numbered (highest priority) set bit */
136	
137	          int bit = __builtin_ctz(status);
138	          return i * INTMUX_IRQS_PER_GROUP + bit;
139	        }
140	    }
141	
142	  return -1;
143	}

149	/****************************************************************************
150	 * Name: riscv_dispatch_irq
151	 *
152	 * Description:
153	 *   Dispatch an interrupt based on the mcause value.
154	 *
155	 *   This function is called from the NuttX RISC-V common interrupt
156	 *   handling path (riscv_doirq -> riscv_dispatch_irq) when the mcause
157	 *   indicates an interrupt (bit 31 set).
158	 *
159	 *   For the RV1126B HPMCU:
160	 *     - mcause == 7  (IRQ_M_TIMER): machine timer interrupt
161	 *     - mcause == 11 (IRQ_M_EXT):   machine external interrupt
162	 *       (routed through INTMUX)
163	 *
164	 * Input Parameters:
165	 *   mcause - The value of the mcause CSR
166	 *   regs   - Pointer to the saved register context
167	 *
168	 * Returned Value:
169	 *   Pointer to the (possibly new) register context after dispatch.
170	 *
171	 ****************************************************************************/
172	
173	void *riscv_dispatch_irq(uintptr_t mcause, uintreg_t *regs)
174	{
175	  uintptr_t cause;
176	
177	  if ((mcause & MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT) == 0)
178	    {
179	      /* Synchronous exceptions must go through riscv_doirq() so NuttX can
180	       * advance mepc for ecall and handle context switching properly.
181	       */
182	
183	      regs = riscv_doirq((int)mcause, regs);
184	      return regs;
185	    }
186	
187	  /* Interrupt: strip the interrupt bit to get the cause code */
188	
189	  cause = mcause & ~MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT;
190	
191	  if (cause == IRQ_M_TIMER)
192	    {
193	      /* Machine timer interrupt -- call the NuttX timer handler */
194	
195	      up_timer_int();
196	    }
197	  else if (cause == IRQ_M_EXT)
198	    {
199	      /* Machine external interrupt -- scan INTMUX for active IRQs */
200	
201	      int irq;
202	
203	      /* Signal IPIC Start of Interrupt */
204	
205	      rv1126b_ipic_soi();
206	
207	      /* Scan for active IRQs -- handle all pending IRQs in this group */
208	
209	      while ((irq = rv1126b_get_active_irq()) >= 0)
210	        {
211	          /* Dispatch through the NuttX IRQ dispatch table.
212	           * riscv_doirq() handles context switch bookkeeping and
213	           * returns the (possibly updated) regs pointer.
214	           */
215	
216	          regs = riscv_doirq(irq, regs);
217	        }
218	
219	      /* Signal IPIC End of Interrupt */
220	
221	      rv1126b_ipic_eoi();
222	    }
223	  else
224	    {
225	      /* Unexpected interrupt cause -- spin */
226	
227	      for (; ; );
228	    }
229	
230	  return regs;
231	}

199	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_SRR_UR | RV1126B_UART_SRR_RFR |
200	           RV1126B_UART_SRR_XFR, UART_SRR(base));
201	
202	  /* Disable all interrupts */
203	
204	  putreg32(0, UART_IER(base));
205	
206	  /* Enable FIFO, reset TX and RX FIFOs */
207	
208	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_FCR_FIFOE | RV1126B_UART_FCR_RFIFOR |
209	           RV1126B_UART_FCR_XFIFOR, UART_FCR(base));
210	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_FCR_FIFOE | RV1126B_UART_FCR_TFT_TWO |
211	           RV1126B_UART_FCR_RT_HALF, UART_FCR(base));
212	
213	  /* Set baud rate */
214	
215	  divisor = priv->clk_rate / 16 / priv->baud;
216	
217	  /* Enable DLAB to access divisor latch registers */
218	
219	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_LCR_DLAB, UART_LCR(base));
220	  putreg32(divisor & 0xff, UART_DLL(base));

23	/****************************************************************************
24	 * RV1126B HPMCU IRQ dispatch for NuttX
25	 *
26	 * This file implements the RISC-V interrupt dispatch logic for the
27	 * RV1126B HPMCU.  The SCR1 core uses the IPIC (CSR 0xbf0..0xbf7) for
28	 * interrupt prioritization and EOI/SOI handshaking, and the INTMUX
29	 * for external interrupt routing.
30	 *
31	 * Dispatch flow:
32	 *   1. Trap entry (rv1126b_head.S g_traps) saves context and calls
33	 *      riscv_dispatch_irq(mcause, regs).
34	 *   2. riscv_dispatch_irq() identifies the interrupt type and:
35	 *      - For timer interrupts (mcause=7): calls up_timer_int()
36	 *        and returns regs.
37	 *      - For external interrupts (mcause=11): scans INTMUX status
38	 *        registers to find the active IRQs, then dispatches each
39	 *        via riscv_doirq(irq, regs) (which handles context switch
40	 *        bookkeeping), wrapped by IPIC SOI/EOI.
41	 *   3. The returned regs pointer is used by the assembly trap exit
42	 *      to restore the (possibly switched) context.
43	 ****************************************************************************/
44

111	/****************************************************************************
112	 * Name: rv1126b_get_active_irq
113	 *
114	 * Description:
115	 *   Scan the INTMUX status registers to find the highest-priority
116	 *   active (pending and enabled) IRQ.
117	 *
118	 * Returned Value:
119	 *   IRQ number (0..255), or -1 if no active IRQ is found.
120	 *
121	 ****************************************************************************/
122	
123	static int rv1126b_get_active_irq(void)
124	{
125	  int i;
126	  unsigned int status;
127	
128	  for (i = 0; i < INTMUX_NGROUPS; i++)
129	    {
130	      status = getreg32(RV1126B_INTMUX_BASE +
131	                         RV1126B_INTMUX_STATUS_OFFSET +
132	                         (i * RV1126B_INTMUX_GROUP_STRIDE));
133	      if (status != 0)
134	        {
135	          /* Find the lowest-numbered (highest priority) set bit */
136	
137	          int bit = __builtin_ctz(status);
138	          return i * INTMUX_IRQS_PER_GROUP + bit;
139	        }
140	    }
141	
142	  return -1;
143	}

149	/****************************************************************************
150	 * Name: riscv_dispatch_irq
151	 *
152	 * Description:
153	 *   Dispatch an interrupt based on the mcause value.
154	 *
155	 *   This function is called from the NuttX RISC-V common interrupt
156	 *   handling path (riscv_doirq -> riscv_dispatch_irq) when the mcause
157	 *   indicates an interrupt (bit 31 set).
158	 *
159	 *   For the RV1126B HPMCU:
160	 *     - mcause == 7  (IRQ_M_TIMER): machine timer interrupt
161	 *     - mcause == 11 (IRQ_M_EXT):   machine external interrupt
162	 *       (routed through INTMUX)
163	 *
164	 * Input Parameters:
165	 *   mcause - The value of the mcause CSR
166	 *   regs   - Pointer to the saved register context
167	 *
168	 * Returned Value:
169	 *   Pointer to the (possibly new) register context after dispatch.
170	 *
171	 ****************************************************************************/
172	
173	void *riscv_dispatch_irq(uintptr_t mcause, uintreg_t *regs)
174	{
175	  uintptr_t cause;
176	
177	  if ((mcause & MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT) == 0)
178	    {
179	      /* Synchronous exceptions must go through riscv_doirq() so NuttX can
180	       * advance mepc for ecall and handle context switching properly.
181	       */
182	
183	      regs = riscv_doirq((int)mcause, regs);
184	      return regs;
185	    }
186	
187	  /* Interrupt: strip the interrupt bit to get the cause code */
188	
189	  cause = mcause & ~MCAUSE_INTERRUPT_BIT;
190	
191	  if (cause == IRQ_M_TIMER)
192	    {
193	      /* Machine timer interrupt -- call the NuttX timer handler */
194	
195	      up_timer_int();
196	    }
197	  else if (cause == IRQ_M_EXT)
198	    {
199	      /* Machine external interrupt -- scan INTMUX for active IRQs */
200	
201	      int irq;
202	
203	      /* Signal IPIC Start of Interrupt */
204	
205	      rv1126b_ipic_soi();
206	
207	      /* Scan for active IRQs -- handle all pending IRQs in this group */
208	
209	      while ((irq = rv1126b_get_active_irq()) >= 0)
210	        {
211	          /* Dispatch through the NuttX IRQ dispatch table.
212	           * riscv_doirq() handles context switch bookkeeping and
213	           * returns the (possibly updated) regs pointer.
214	           */
215	
216	          regs = riscv_doirq(irq, regs);
217	        }
218	
219	      /* Signal IPIC End of Interrupt */
220	
221	      rv1126b_ipic_eoi();
222	    }
223	  else
224	    {
225	      /* Unexpected interrupt cause -- spin */
226	
227	      for (; ; );
228	    }
229	
230	  return regs;
231	}

160	static bool rv1126b_dcache_init(void)
161	{
162	  volatile uint32_t *grf_cache_start =
163	    (volatile uint32_t *)GRF_HPMCU_CACHE_ADDR_START;
164	  volatile uint32_t *grf_cache_end =
165	    (volatile uint32_t *)GRF_HPMCU_CACHE_ADDR_END;
166	  volatile uint32_t *dcache_ctrl =
167	    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_CACHE_CTRL;
168	  volatile uint32_t *dcache_status =
169	    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_CACHE_STATUS;
170	  volatile uint32_t *dcache_stb =
171	    (volatile uint32_t *)DCACHE_STB_TIMEOUT_CTRL;
172	  volatile uint32_t timeout = RV1126B_DIAG_POLL_TIMEOUT;
173	
174	  /* Set the uncache region to cover peripheral address space */
175	
176	  *grf_cache_start = 0x20000;
177	  *grf_cache_end   = 0x23000;
178	
179	  /* Enable DCache: cache_en=1, stb_entry=7, stb_timeout_en=1 */
180	
181	  *dcache_ctrl |= DCACHE_CACHE_EN_BIT |
182	                  DCACHE_CACHE_ENTRY_THRESH |
183	                  DCACHE_STB_TIMEOUT_EN_BIT;
184	
185	  /* Enable store buffer timeout */
186	
187	  *dcache_stb = 1;
188	
189	  /* Wait for cache initialization to finish */
190	
191	  while ((*dcache_status & DCACHE_INIT_FINISH_BIT) == 0)
192	    {
193	      if (timeout-- == 0)
194	        {
195	          return false;
196	        }
197	    }
198	
199	  /* Clear bypass to enable caching */
200	
201	  *dcache_ctrl &= ~DCACHE_CACHE_BYPASS_BIT;
202	  return true;
203	}

42	/* PLL configuration registers */

44	#define TOPCRU_BASE           RV1126B_TOPCRU_BASE
45	
46	/* GPLL (General PLL) registers at TOPCRU
47	 *
48	 * SDK-confirmed layout (rv1126b.h TOPCRU_REG):
49	 *   AUPLL_CON[5] at offset 0x0000 (5 registers, 20 bytes)
50	 *   GPLL_CON[5]  at offset 0x0020
51	 *
52	 * GPLL_CON0: PLL divisor, multiplier, and lock status
53	 *   Bit 31: LOCK (read-only, 1 = PLL is locked)
54	 *
55	 * PLL output = (24 MHz / refdiv) * fbdiv / postdiv1 / postdiv2
56	 * For 1188 MHz: refdiv=1, fbdiv=99, postdiv1=2, postdiv2=1
57	 *   (24/1) * 99 / 2 = 1188 MHz
58	 */
59	
60	#define GPLL_CON0_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x0020)  /* GPLL_CON[0] */
61	#define GPLL_CON1_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x0024)  /* GPLL_CON[1] */
62	#define GPLL_CON2_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x0028)  /* GPLL_CON[2] */
63	#define GPLL_CON3_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x002c)  /* GPLL_CON[3] */
64	#define GPLL_CON4_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x0030)  /* GPLL_CON[4] */
65	
66	/* HPMCU clock source selection
67	 * CLK_HPMCU is a gated clock from aclk_bus_root (no mux/divider).
68	 * SDK-verified: SCR1_CORE_FREQUECY = 396 MHz (GPLL 1188 MHz / 3).
69	 * The divider is configured by A-core/bootrom; HPMCU does not need
70	 * to write to CORECRU CLKSEL_CON00 (those bits belong to A53 core).
71	 */
72	
73	/* SDK-verified: GPLL lock status is at GPLL_CON[2] bit 10 (TOPCRU + 0x28) */
74	
75	#define GPLL_LOCK_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x0028)
76	#define GPLL_LOCK_SHIFT       10
77	#define GPLL_LOCK_MASK        (1 << GPLL_LOCK_SHIFT)

83	/****************************************************************************
84	 * Name: rv1126b_wait_pll_lock
85	 *
86	 * Description:
87	 *   Wait for the PLL to achieve lock by polling the lock bit.
88	 *
89	 * Returned Value:
90	 *   true if PLL locked within the timeout, false otherwise.
91	 *
92	 ****************************************************************************/
93	
94	static bool rv1126b_wait_pll_lock(uint32_t pll_lock_addr)
95	{
96	  volatile uint32_t timeout = 1000000;
97	
98	  while (timeout > 0)
99	    {
100	      if (getreg32(pll_lock_addr) & GPLL_LOCK_MASK)
101	        {
102	          return true;  /* PLL locked */
103	        }
104	
105	      timeout--;
106	    }
107	
108	  return false;  /* Timeout -- PLL did not lock */
109	}

112	 * Name: rv1126b_ensure_gpll_locked
113	 *
114	 * Description:
115	 *   Verify that GPLL is already locked at 1188 MHz.  In an AMP
116	 *   environment the Linux A-core (or bootrom) will have configured
117	 *   GPLL before the HPMCU starts.  We do NOT reconfigure GPLL here
118	 *   to avoid interfering with other cores that depend on it.
119	 *
120	 *   If GPLL is not locked, let the caller return without changing clocks.
121	 *
122	 ****************************************************************************/

124	static bool rv1126b_ensure_gpll_locked(void)
125	{
126	  if (!rv1126b_wait_pll_lock(GPLL_LOCK_ADDR))
127	    {
128	      return false;
129	    }
130	
131	  return true;
132	}

135	 * Name: rv1126b_set_hpmcu_clock
136	 *
137	 * Description:
138	 *   Verify HPMCU clock is already configured to 396 MHz.
139	 *
140	 *   On the RV1126B, CLK_HPMCU is a gated clock sourced from aclk_bus_root
141	 *   (confirmed by the Linux CRU driver: GATE(CLK_HPMCU, "clk_hpmcu",
142	 *   "aclk_bus_root", ...)).  The clock source selection and divider are
143	 *   configured by the A-core Linux or bootrom before the HPMCU starts.
144	 *
145	 *   SDK-verified: SCR1_CORE_FREQUECY = 396 MHz, GPLL = 1188 MHz.
146	 *   The ratio 1188/3 = 396 MHz matches, but we do NOT write to
147	 *   CORECRU CLKSEL_CON00 because bits [5:0] are allocated to the A53
148	 *   core clock (CLK_CORE_PVTPLL_SRC_SEL, CLK_CORE_SRC_SEL) per the
149	 *   SDK header rv1126b.h, not to the HPMCU.
150	 *
151	 ****************************************************************************/
152	
153	static void rv1126b_set_hpmcu_clock(void)
154	{
155	  /* HPMCU clock is pre-configured by A-core/bootrom.
156	   * No register writes needed -- aclk_bus_root is already set.
157	   * If in the future this needs explicit configuration, the correct
158	   * register and bit fields must be determined from the TRM.
159	   */
160	}

168	 *
169	 * Description:
170	 *   Configure the system clocks for the RV1126B HPMCU.
171	 *
172	 *   This function is called from rv1126b_start() very early in the boot
173	 *   sequence.  In an AMP environment, GPLL is already configured by the
174	 *   Linux A-core or bootrom.  This function:
175	 *     1. Verifies GPLL is locked at 1188 MHz (does NOT reconfigure it)
176	 *     2. Sets HPMCU core clock to 396 MHz (GPLL / 3)
177	 *
178	 ****************************************************************************/
179	
180	void rv1126b_clockconfig(void)
181	{
182	  /* Step 1: Verify GPLL is locked (already configured by A-core/bootrom).
183	   * Do NOT reconfigure GPLL to avoid disrupting Linux on the A-core.
184	   * If GPLL is not locked, leave clocks unchanged.
185	   */
186	
187	  if (!rv1126b_ensure_gpll_locked())
188	    {
189	      return;
190	    }
191	
192	  /* Step 2: HPMCU clock is pre-configured to 396 MHz (GPLL / 3) by
193	   * the A-core or bootrom.  CLK_HPMCU is a gate from aclk_bus_root;
194	   * no explicit divider configuration is needed or safe here.
195	   */
196	
197	  rv1126b_set_hpmcu_clock();

108	
109	static void rv1126b_uart5_enable_clock(void)
110	{
111	  /* Select 24 MHz oscillator as UART5 source clock.
112	   * CLKSEL_CON14 at TOPCRU + 0x338:
113	   *   Bits [15:13] = SCLK_UART5_SRC_SEL (0 = XIN_OSC0 / 24 MHz)
114	   *   Bits [12:8]  = SCLK_UART5_SRC_DIV (0 = divide by 1)
115	   * Use Rockchip high-word write-mask semantics so unrelated fields are not
116	   * affected.
117	   */
118	
119	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE((0x7u << 13) | (0x1fu << 8), 0),
120	           TOPCRU_BASE + 0x338);
121	
122	  /* Enable UART5 source clock gate (SCLK_UART5_SRC_GATE in GATE_CON01)
123	   * Bit 14 of GATE_CON01 at TOPCRU + 0x804.
124	   * Gate bits are active-high disables, so write data 0 to enable.
125	   */
126	
127	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE(RV1126B_SCLK_UART5_SRC_GATE, 0),
128	           CONSOLE_SCLK_GATE_REG);
129	
130	  /* Enable UART5 peripheral clock gate (PCLK_UART5_GATE in GATE_CON04)
131	   * Bit 13 of GATE_CON04 at BUSCRU + 0x810.
132	   */
133	
134	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE(RV1126B_PCLK_UART5_GATE, 0),
135	           CONSOLE_PCLK_GATE_REG);
136	}

159	/****************************************************************************
160	 * Name: rv1126b_uart5_config_pins
161	 *
162	 * Description:
163	 *   Configure GPIO4_A6 (TX) and GPIO4_A7 (RX) pin mux for UART5 M0
164	 *   function.  The IOC (I/O Controller) registers select the pin function.
165	 *
166	 *   SDK-verified mapping: UART5 M0 -> GPIO4_PA6 FUNC5, GPIO4_PA7 FUNC5.
167	 *
168	 ****************************************************************************/
169	
170	static void rv1126b_uart5_config_pins(void)
171	{
172	  /* GPIO4_A6 = UART5_TXM0 (FUNC5)
173	   * GPIO4_A7 = UART5_RXM0 (FUNC5)
174	   *
175	   * Both pins share GPIO4A_IOMUX_SEL_1 at GPIO4_IOC_BASE + 0x84:
176	   *   Bits [11:8]  = GPIO4_A6 function select (5 = UART5)
177	   *   Bits [15:12] = GPIO4_A7 function select (5 = UART5)
178	   *
179	   * SDK-verified: rv1126b.h GPIO4A6_SEL_SHIFT=8, GPIO4A7_SEL_SHIFT=12
180	   * Linux DTS: <4 RK_PA7 5 &pcfg_pull_up>, <4 RK_PA6 5 &pcfg_pull_up>
181	   * High-word masked write value: 0xff005500.
182	   */
183	
184	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE((0xfu << 8) | (0xfu << 12),
185	                                 (5u << 8) | (5u << 12)),
186	           GPIO4_IOC_BASE + 0x84);  /* GPIO4A_IOMUX_SEL_1 */
187	
188	  /* Enable pull-up on UART5 TX (GPIO4_PA6) and RX (GPIO4_PA7) pins
189	   * to prevent spurious characters when line is undriven.
190	   * GPIO4A_PULL at GPIO4_IOC_BASE + 0x340:
191	   *   bits [13:12] = GPIO4_A6 pull (1 = pull-up)
192	   *   bits [15:14] = GPIO4_A7 pull (1 = pull-up)
193	   * SDK/HAL-confirmed combined high-word write value: 0xf0005000.
194	   */
195	
196	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE((0x3u << 12) | (0x3u << 14),
197	                                 (1u << 12) | (1u << 14)),
198	           GPIO4_IOC_BASE + 0x340);  /* GPIO4A_PULL */
199	}

201	/****************************************************************************
202	 * Name: rv1126b_uart5_init_hw
203	 *
204	 * Description:
205	 *   Initialize UART5 hardware: reset, set baud rate, configure 8N1, enable
206	 *   FIFO.
207	 *
208	 ****************************************************************************/
209	
210	static void rv1126b_uart5_init_hw(void)
211	{
212	  /* Software reset UART5 */
213	
214	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_SRR_UR | RV1126B_UART_SRR_RFR |
215	           RV1126B_UART_SRR_XFR, UART_SRR(UART_BASE));
216	
217	  /* Disable all interrupts */
218	
219	  putreg32(0, UART_IER(UART_BASE));
220	
221	  /* Enable FIFO, reset TX and RX FIFOs */
222	
223	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_FCR_FIFOE | RV1126B_UART_FCR_RFIFOR |
224	           RV1126B_UART_FCR_XFIFOR, UART_FCR(UART_BASE));
225	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_FCR_FIFOE | RV1126B_UART_FCR_TFT_TWO |
226	           RV1126B_UART_FCR_RT_HALF, UART_FCR(UART_BASE));
227	
228	  /* Set baud rate: enable DLAB, write divisor, disable DLAB
229	   * Divisor is computed from CONSOLE_CLK_RATE and CONSOLE_BAUD_RATE
230	   * in rv1126b_config.h (Kconfig-derived, default 1500000 baud).
231	   */
232	
233	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_LCR_DLAB, UART_LCR(UART_BASE));
234	  putreg32(CONSOLE_DIVISOR & 0xff, UART_DLL(UART_BASE));
235	  putreg32((CONSOLE_DIVISOR >> 8) & 0xff, UART_DLH(UART_BASE));
236	
237	  /* Set line control: 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit (8N1) */
238	
239	  putreg32(RV1126B_UART_LCR_DLS_8 | RV1126B_UART_LCR_STOP_1,
240	           UART_LCR(UART_BASE));
241	}

53	 *   Bit 31: LOCK (read-only, 1 = PLL is locked)
54	 *
55	 * PLL output = (24 MHz / refdiv) * fbdiv / postdiv1 / postdiv2
56	 * For 1188 MHz: refdiv=1, fbdiv=99, postdiv1=2, postdiv2=1
57	 *   (24/1) * 99 / 2 = 1188 MHz
58	 */

61	#define GPLL_CON1_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x0024)  /* GPLL_CON[1] */
62	#define GPLL_CON2_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x0028)  /* GPLL_CON[2] */
63	#define GPLL_CON3_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x002c)  /* GPLL_CON[3] */
64	#define GPLL_CON4_ADDR        (TOPCRU_BASE + 0x0030)  /* GPLL_CON[4] */

67	 * CLK_HPMCU is a gated clock from aclk_bus_root (no mux/divider).

71	 */

110	{
111	  /* Select 24 MHz oscillator as UART5 source clock.
112	   * CLKSEL_CON14 at TOPCRU + 0x338:
113	   *   Bits [15:13] = SCLK_UART5_SRC_SEL (0 = XIN_OSC0 / 24 MHz)
114	   *   Bits [12:8]  = SCLK_UART5_SRC_DIV (0 = divide by 1)
115	   * Use Rockchip high-word write-mask semantics so unrelated fields are not
116	   * affected.
117	   */
118	
119	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE((0x7u << 13) | (0x1fu << 8), 0),
120	           TOPCRU_BASE + 0x338);
121	
122	  /* Enable UART5 source clock gate (SCLK_UART5_SRC_GATE in GATE_CON01)
123	   * Bit 14 of GATE_CON01 at TOPCRU + 0x804.
124	   * Gate bits are active-high disables, so write data 0 to enable.
125	   */
126	
127	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE(RV1126B_SCLK_UART5_SRC_GATE, 0),
128	           CONSOLE_SCLK_GATE_REG);
129	
130	  /* Enable UART5 peripheral clock gate (PCLK_UART5_GATE in GATE_CON04)
131	   * Bit 13 of GATE_CON04 at BUSCRU + 0x810.
132	   */
133	
134	  putreg32(RV1126B_HIWORD_UPDATE(RV1126B_PCLK_UART5_GATE, 0),
135	           CONSOLE_PCLK_GATE_REG);

227	
228	  /* Set baud rate: enable DLAB, write divisor, disable DLAB

133	### 5.3 link.lds 内存布局（关键参考）
134	
135	```ld
136	OUTPUT_ARCH( "riscv" )
137	ENTRY(_start)
138	
139	MEMORY {
140	    /* mcu VMA on ddr space:
141	       A53.bin: 0x48c00000, 8KB
142	       mcu:     0x48c02000, 232KB (0x3a000)
143	       mcu_log: 0x48c0c000, 16KB */
144	    RAM (rwx)         : ORIGIN = 0x48c02000, LENGTH = 0x3a000
145	    LINUX_RPMSG (rxw) : ORIGIN = 0x48c3c000, LENGTH = 0x20000
146	}
147	```
148	
149	**关键参数：**
150	
151	- HPMCU 运行地址：`0x48c02000`
152	- HPMCU 可用内存：232KB（`0x3a000`）
153	- Linux RPMsg 共享内存：`0x48c3c000`，128KB（`0x20000`）
154	- A53 固件区：`0x48c00000`，8KB
155	- HPMCU 日志区：`0x48c0c000`，16KB

220	## 7. 最高优先级风险
221	
222	### 7.1 UART0 vs UART4 配置冲突
223	
224	- **问题**：当前 `rv1126b_serial.c` / `rv1126b_lowputc.c` 可能默认使用 UART0，但 SDK 约定 HPMCU 调试串口为 UART4。
225	- **影响**：如果 UART 配置不正确，无法看到任何串口输出，调试完全受阻。
226	- **参考**：SDK RT-Thread BSP `drivers/` 中的 UART 驱动使用 UART4。
227	
228	### 7.2 GRF_SYS 基址矛盾
229	
230	- **问题**：`hardware/rv1126b_memorymap.h` 中 GRF_SYS 基地址可能与 SDK 定义不一致。
231	- **影响**：时钟、GPIO 复用等寄存器操作全部出错。
232	- **对策**：必须与 SDK `hal_conf.h` 或 Rockchip TRM 逐一核对。
233	
234	### 7.3 GPLL 初始化策略冲突
235	
236	- **问题**：`rv1126b_clockconfig.c` 中 GPLL 初始化逻辑可能与 SDK 方案不同（是否需要等待 PLL 锁定、分频系数等）。
237	- **影响**：时钟频率不正确导致 UART 波特率偏差、定时器不准。
238	- **参考**：SDK RT-Thread BSP `board/` 目录中的时钟初始化代码。
239	
240	### 7.4 SCR1/IPIC 私有中断路径
241	
242	- **问题**：RV1126B HPMCU 使用 SCR1 CPU 核心，其中断控制器为 IPIC（Internal Programmable Interrupt Controller），不同于标准 RISC-V PLIC/CLINT。
243	- **影响**：当前 NuttX RISC-V 中断框架可能需要适配 IPIC。
244	- **参考**：`hardware/rv1126b_intmux.h` 和 SDK RT-Thread 的中断处理代码。
245	
246	### 7.5 hpmcu_start.bin / 打包链路
247	
248	- **问题**：open-vela 编译输出的 ELF/BIN 如何打包成 AMP 框架可加载的 `hpmcu_start.bin`？
249	- **影响**：即使编译成功，也无法实际部署运行。
250	- **参考**：SDK `mkimage.sh` 和 `amp.its`。
251	
252	### 7.6 RPMsg 共享内存 Size 不一致
253	
254	- **问题**：`link.lds` 中 `LINUX_RPMSG` 段大小（128KB）需与 Linux 端 DTS 配置完全一致。
255	- **影响**：不一致会导致 Linux 与 HPMCU IPC 通信失败或内存踩踏。
256	
257	### 7.7 模板占位
258	
259	- **问题**：`contest2026_000`、`team000` 等占位符未清理。
260	- **影响**：构建路径错误、Kconfig 解析失败。

### 5.2 构建方式

RT-Thread 使用 SCons 构建系统（`SConstruct` + `SConscript`）。打包通过 `mkimage.sh` 脚本完成。

### 5.3 link.lds 内存布局（关键参考）

```ld
OUTPUT_ARCH( "riscv" )
ENTRY(_start)

MEMORY {
    /* mcu VMA on ddr space:
       A53.bin: 0x48c00000, 8KB
       mcu:     0x48c02000, 232KB (0x3a000)
       mcu_log: 0x48c0c000, 16KB */
    RAM (rwx)         : ORIGIN = 0x48c02000, LENGTH = 0x3a000
    LINUX_RPMSG (rxw) : ORIGIN = 0x48c3c000, LENGTH = 0x20000
}
```

**关键参数：**

- HPMCU 运行地址：`0x48c02000`
- HPMCU 可用内存：232KB（`0x3a000`）
- Linux RPMsg 共享内存：`0x48c3c000`，128KB（`0x20000`）
- A53 固件区：`0x48c00000`，8KB
- HPMCU 日志区：`0x48c0c000`，16KB

### 5.4 amp.its / amp_mcu.its

- `$SDK/rtos/bsp/rockchip/rv1126b-mcu/Image/amp.its`：AMP 镜像打包描述文件
- `$SDK/device/rockchip/.chips/rv1126b/amp_mcu.its`：MCU AMP 镜像配置

### 5.5 hpmcu_start.bin

打包流程生成 `hpmcu_start.bin`，由 Linux 端 AMP 框架加载到 HPMCU 运行地址。

### 5.6 UART4 1.5Mbaud

SDK 默认 HPMCU 调试串口为 **UART4**，波特率 **1500000 (1.5Mbps)**。这是 Rockchip MCU 的典型配置。

### 5.7 HPMCU 396MHz

HPMCU 运行频率：**396MHz**，由 CRU 从 GPLL 分频得到。

### 5.8 Rockchip AMP 启动链路

```
DDR 加载 A53.bin
    → A53 (Linux) 启动
    → AMP 框架加载 hpmcu_start.bin 到 0x48c02000
    → HPMCU 开始执行 _start
```

DTS 参考：`$SDK/kernel-6.1/arch/arm64/boot/dts/rockchip/rv1126b-amp.dtsi`

### 5.9 RPMsg / Mailbox / OpenAMP 线索

- SDK 中存在 RPMsg 共享内存区域定义（`LINUX_RPMSG` 段）
- Linux DTS 中有 AMP 相关配置
- RT-Thread BSP 中可能包含 OpenAMP/RPMsg 组件（需进一步确认 `components/` 目录）
- 这是 Linux 与 HPMCU 之间 IPC 的基础机制

| 测试 | 硬件测试验证 |

## 7. 最高优先级风险

### 7.1 UART0 vs UART4 配置冲突

- **问题**：当前 `rv1126b_serial.c` / `rv1126b_lowputc.c` 可能默认使用 UART0，但 SDK 约定 HPMCU 调试串口为 UART4。
- **影响**：如果 UART 配置不正确，无法看到任何串口输出，调试完全受阻。
- **参考**：SDK RT-Thread BSP `drivers/` 中的 UART 驱动使用 UART4。

### 7.2 GRF_SYS 基址矛盾

- **问题**：`hardware/rv1126b_memorymap.h` 中 GRF_SYS 基地址可能与 SDK 定义不一致。
- **影响**：时钟、GPIO 复用等寄存器操作全部出错。
- **对策**：必须与 SDK `hal_conf.h` 或 Rockchip TRM 逐一核对。

### 7.3 GPLL 初始化策略冲突

- **问题**：`rv1126b_clockconfig.c` 中 GPLL 初始化逻辑可能与 SDK 方案不同（是否需要等待 PLL 锁定、分频系数等）。
- **影响**：时钟频率不正确导致 UART 波特率偏差、定时器不准。
- **参考**：SDK RT-Thread BSP `board/` 目录中的时钟初始化代码。

### 7.4 SCR1/IPIC 私有中断路径

- **问题**：RV1126B HPMCU 使用 SCR1 CPU 核心，其中断控制器为 IPIC（Internal Programmable Interrupt Controller），不同于标准 RISC-V PLIC/CLINT。
- **影响**：当前 NuttX RISC-V 中断框架可能需要适配 IPIC。
- **参考**：`hardware/rv1126b_intmux.h` 和 SDK RT-Thread 的中断处理代码。

### 7.5 hpmcu_start.bin / 打包链路

- **问题**：open-vela 编译输出的 ELF/BIN 如何打包成 AMP 框架可加载的 `hpmcu_start.bin`？
- **影响**：即使编译成功，也无法实际部署运行。
- **参考**：SDK `mkimage.sh` 和 `amp.its`。

### 7.6 RPMsg 共享内存 Size 不一致

- **问题**：`link.lds` 中 `LINUX_RPMSG` 段大小（128KB）需与 Linux 端 DTS 配置完全一致。
- **影响**：不一致会导致 Linux 与 HPMCU IPC 通信失败或内存踩踏。

### 7.7 模板占位

- **问题**：`contest2026_000`、`team000` 等占位符未清理。
- **影响**：构建路径错误、Kconfig 解析失败。

1. NSH banner 输出后进入 `readline_fd` → `read(fd0)` → `uart_read`；接收缓冲区为空时阻塞在 `recvsem`。
2. `uart_register` 只注册 inode；第一次 `uart_open` 才执行 `attach` 和 `rxint(true)`。console 因 `isconsole` 跳过 `setup`。
3. banner 正常而输入无反应最符合以下情况：`attach` 表面成功，但硬件 IRQ / INTMUX 未触发，导致 `uart_read` 永远阻塞。
4. 团队 `chip/rv1126b_idle.c` 已有 `up_idle` polling：UART5 RFNE 时调用 `uart_recvchars`。下一步必须确认该文件是否编入最终 ELF，以及最终 `up_idle` 符号是否来自团队实现。
5. `/dev/console` 与 `/dev/ttyS0` 共享同一个 `uart_dev` 双注册通常可用，不是首要根因。
6. 恢复后优先使用 `nm` / `objdump` 验证 `up_idle` 符号，再结合另外两个 Sonnet 调查核对 INTMUX。

### Sonnet SDK 路由调查已完成

- SDK `UART5_IRQn = 61`，团队 `CONSOLE_UART_IRQ = 61` 正确。
- UART5 对应 INTMUX group 1 bit 29；enable 寄存器地址为 `0x20b40004`，status 寄存器地址为 `0x20b40084`。

- SDK UART5 console 同样是 interrupt-driven，不是 polling。

23	/****************************************************************************
24	 * RV1126B HPMCU interrupt controller (INTMUX) for NuttX
25	 *
26	 * The RV1126B HPMCU uses a RISC-V SCR1 core with a local interrupt
27	 * controller (IPIC) and an external interrupt multiplexer (INTMUX).
28	 * External interrupts from peripherals are routed through the INTMUX
29	 * before reaching the machine external interrupt (MEIP) line.
30	 *
31	 * INTMUX register layout:
32	 *   Base: 0x20b40000
33	 *   Enable registers: offset 0x00..0x1C (8 groups x 32 bits = 256 IRQs)
34	 *   Status registers: offset 0x80..0x9C (8 groups x 32 bits)
35	 *
36	 * The IPIC (CSR 0xbf0..0xbf7) is used for EOI/SOI handshaking with the
37	 * SCR1 interrupt controller.
38	 ****************************************************************************/

71	/****************************************************************************
72	 * Name: rv1126b_intmux_enable
73	 *
74	 * Description:
75	 *   Enable a specific IRQ in the INTMUX enable registers.
76	 *   Uses the RV1126B_INTMUX_ENABLE(n) macro from rv1126b_intmux.h.
77	 *
78	 * Input Parameters:
79	 *   irq - IRQ number (0..255)
80	 *
81	 ****************************************************************************/
82	
83	static void rv1126b_intmux_enable(int irq)
84	{
85	  uintptr_t reg = RV1126B_INTMUX_ENABLE(irq);
86	  unsigned int bit = irq % INTMUX_IRQS_PER_GROUP;
87	
88	  putreg32(getreg32(reg) | (1u << bit), reg);
89	}

115	/****************************************************************************
116	 * Name: up_irqinitialize
117	 *
118	 * Description:
119	 *   Initialize the interrupt subsystem for the RV1126B HPMCU.
120	 *   - Disable all INTMUX enables
121	 *   - Set mtvec to the trap vector
122	 *   - Enable machine external interrupts in MIE
123	 *   - Enable global interrupts
124	 *
125	 ****************************************************************************/
126	
127	void up_irqinitialize(void)
128	{
129	  int i;
130	
131	  /* Disable all INTMUX interrupt enables */
132	
133	  for (i = 0; i < INTMUX_NGROUPS; i++)
134	    {
135	      putreg32(0, RV1126B_INTMUX_BASE + RV1126B_INTMUX_ENABLE_OFFSET +
136	                (i * RV1126B_INTMUX_GROUP_STRIDE));
137	    }
138	
139	  /* Enable all IPIC vectors before enabling MEIP.  write_csr() stringifies
140	   * its CSR argument, so these CSR numbers must remain literals.
141	   */
142	
143	  for (i = 0; i < 16; i++)
144	    {
145	      write_csr(0xbf6, i);
146	      write_csr(0xbf7, 1u << 1);
147	    }
148	
149	  /* Note: mtvec is already set to the NuttX trap vector
150	   * (g_traps in rv1126b_head.S) before NuttX code runs.
151	   */
152	
153	  /* Enable machine external interrupts (MEIP) in the mie CSR */
154	
155	  set_csr(mie, MIP_MEIP);
156	
157	  /* Enable global interrupts */
158	
159	  up_irq_enable();
160	}

202	irqstate_t up_irq_enable(void)
203	{

210	      : "r"(MSTATUS_MIE)
211	      : "memory"

132	
133	  for (i = 0; i < INTMUX_NGROUPS; i++)
134	    {
135	      putreg32(0, RV1126B_INTMUX_BASE + RV1126B_INTMUX_ENABLE_OFFSET +

188

194

208

 * NuttX - RV1126B BSP Configuration
 *
 * Console UART selection, clock rate, and baud rate definitions shared
 * between the early lowputc driver and the full serial driver.
 *
 * This BSP uses a custom rv1126b_serial.c driver rather than the generic

 ****************************************************************************/

#ifndef __BOARD_CHIP_RV1126B_CONFIG_H
#define __BOARD_CHIP_RV1126B_CONFIG_H

/****************************************************************************
 * Pre-processor Definitions
 ****************************************************************************/

/* UART configuration
 *
 * This BSP uses a custom rv1126b_serial.c driver rather than the generic
 * 16550 driver.  The console is selected via CONFIG_RV1126B_UART5_CONSOLE
 * defined in the chip Kconfig.
 */

#if defined(CONFIG_RV1126B_UART5_CONSOLE)
#  define HAVE_UART           1
#  define HAVE_SERIAL_CONSOLE 1
#  define CONSOLE_UART        5
#  define CONSOLE_BASE        RV1126B_UART5_BASE
#else
#  define HAVE_UART           0
#  define HAVE_SERIAL_CONSOLE 0
#endif

/* GPIO configuration */

#if defined(CONFIG_DEV_GPIO)
#  define HAVE_GPIO           1
#else
#  define HAVE_GPIO           0
#endif

/* Timer configuration */

#define HAVE_TIMER            1
#define TIMER_FREQUENCY       396000000  /* 396 MHz timer input clock */

/* UART5 source clock rate (24 MHz oscillator, SDK-verified) */

#define CONSOLE_CLK_RATE      24000000

/* Console baud rate and divisor latch value.
 * SDK default for all UARTs on this SoC is 1500000 baud.
 */

#define CONSOLE_BAUD_RATE     1500000

#define CONSOLE_DIVISOR       (CONSOLE_CLK_RATE / 16 / CONSOLE_BAUD_RATE)

#endif /* __BOARD_CHIP_RV1126B_CONFIG_H */

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: riscv_lowputc
 *
 * Description:
 *   Output one character on UART5 using polled I/O.
 *   This function is used for very early console output before the full
 *   serial driver is initialized.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

void riscv_lowputc(char ch)
{
  uint32_t timeout = RV1126B_UART_TX_TIMEOUT;

  /* Wait until TX FIFO is not full */

  while (!(getreg32(UART_USR(UART_BASE)) & RV1126B_UART_USR_TFNF))
    {
      if (timeout-- == 0)
        {
          return;
        }
    }

  /* Write the character to the transmit holding register */

  putreg32((uint32_t)ch, UART_THR(UART_BASE));
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: riscv_lowgetc
 *
 * Description:
 *   Read one character from UART5 using polled I/O.
 *   Returns -1 if no character is available.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int riscv_lowgetc(void)
{
  /* Check if RX FIFO has data */

  if (!(getreg32(UART_USR(UART_BASE)) & RV1126B_UART_USR_RFNE))
    {
      return -1;
    }

  /* Read the character from the receive buffer register */

  return (int)(getreg32(UART_RBR(UART_BASE)) & 0xff);
}

#include <rtthread.h>
#include "int_mux.h"

void rt_hw_interrupt_active(int vector)
{
    unsigned int index, set;
    unsigned int temp;

    index = vector / 32;
    set = vector % 32;
    temp = *(unsigned int *)(INT_MUX + index * 4);
    *(unsigned int *)(INT_MUX + index * 4) = (1 << set) | temp;
}

void rt_hw_interrupt_deactive(int vector)
{
    unsigned int index, set;

    index = vector / 32;
    set = vector % 32;
    *(unsigned int *)(INT_MUX + index * 4) &= ~(1 << set);
}

rt_uint32_t rt_hw_interrupt_get_active(void)
{
    rt_uint32_t cause = -1;
    int i, n;
    unsigned int int_reg;

    for (i = 0; i < INT_GROUP; i++)
    {
        if (*(unsigned int *)(INT_MUX + INT_MUX_GROUP + i * 4))
            break;
    }

    if (i < INT_GROUP)
    {
        int_reg = *(unsigned int *)(INT_MUX + INT_MUX_GROUP + i * 4);
        for (n = 0; n < 32; n++)
        {
            if (((int_reg >> n) & 0x1) == 0x1)
                break;
        }

        cause = i * 32 + n;
    }

    return cause;
}

#include <rtthread.h>
#include "timer.h"
#include "riscv_csr_encoding.h"

static struct timer_cmp_t timer_cmp;

/* REG ADDR DEF end */
#define word32  *(volatile unsigned int *)
#define word16  *(volatile unsigned short *)
#define word8   *(volatile unsigned char *)

static void _reset_mtime()
{
    word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIME) = 0x00;
    word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIMEH) = 0x00;
}

static void _reset_mtimecmp()
{
    word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIMECMP) = 0x00;
    word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIMECMPH) = 0x00;
}

static void _write_mtime_ctrl(unsigned int t)
{
    word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIME_CTRL) = t;
}

static void _write_mtime_div(unsigned int t)
{
    word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIME_DIV) = t;
}

static void _write_mtimecmp(unsigned int t)
{
    word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIMECMP) = t;
}

static void _write_mtimecmph(unsigned int t)
{
    word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIMECMPH) = t;
}

static void _write_mtime(unsigned int t)
{
    word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIME) = t;
}

static void _write_mtimeh(unsigned int t)
{
    word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIMEH) = t;
}

static unsigned int _read_mtimecmp()
{
    return word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIMECMP);
}

static unsigned int _read_mtimecmph()
{
    return word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIMECMPH);
}

static unsigned int _read_mtime()
{
    return word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIME);
}

static unsigned int _read_mtimeh()
{
    return word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIMEH);
}

static unsigned int _read_mtime_ctrl()
{
    return word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIME_CTRL);
}

static unsigned int _read_mtime_div()
{
    return word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIME_DIV);
}

static void _run_timer()
{
    unsigned int temp;
    temp = word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIME_CTRL);
    temp |= (1 << SCR1_MTIME_CTRL_EN);
    word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIME_CTRL) = temp;
}

static void _stop_timer()
{
    unsigned int temp;
    temp = word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIME_CTRL);
    temp &= (~(1 << SCR1_MTIME_CTRL_EN));
    word32(CTIMER_BASE + CTIMER_MTIME_CTRL) = temp;
}

void sysTick_stop(void)
{
    _stop_timer();
}

void _update_timer(void)
{
    clear_csr(mie, MIP_MTIP);
    timer_cmp.time_cmp = ((uint64_t)_read_mtimeh() << 32) | _read_mtime();
    timer_cmp.time_cmp += timer_cmp.step;
    _write_mtimecmp(timer_cmp.time_cmp & 0xffffffff);
    _write_mtimecmph((timer_cmp.time_cmp >> 32) & 0xffffffff);
    set_csr(mie, MIP_MTIP);
}

void sysTick_config(unsigned int ticks)
{
    _stop_timer();
    _reset_mtime();
    _reset_mtimecmp();
    _write_mtime_div(SCR1_SYS_TIMER_DIV);
    _write_mtimecmp(ticks / SCR1_SYS_TIMER_DIV);
    timer_cmp.time_cmp = ticks / SCR1_SYS_TIMER_DIV;
    timer_cmp.step = ticks / SCR1_SYS_TIMER_DIV;
    set_csr(mie, MIP_MTIP);
    _run_timer();
}

{
